chapters.title: Chapter 1377: A sword divine
paragraphs: "What in the hell," Jest muttered, his forehead breaking into waves of sweat.
"That is indeed true, kid. Welcome to the Yang Hell Flame Sword Realm. I am Sword Divine Yuan." A voice came from behind Jest, taking him by surprise.
There was just no way to describe the hell he appeared in. All around him, only scorching hot fire could be seen, burning with the fury of an undying fury.
Jest, who already had a level 5 heavenly sword energy, felt like an ant standing in such an environment.
Turning around, his gaze met that of a handsome redhead human with a pair of razor-sharp eyebrows.
"Is this really your sword realm?" Jest asked, clearly in disbelief. To him, a sword realm is basically a small manifestation of the swordsman’s understanding of their sword path.
There is just no way it should be this vast and powerful.

"I know what you are wondering, kid. In my opinion, throw away all you know of swordsmanship because when you awaken the Divine sword energy and finally become a Sword Divine like me, everything changes.

Whatever you know of swordsmanship, see it as you in the lower realm. You are now in the higher realm, so please don’t even for one second consider the idea that you can muster any resistance against me."
Jest nodded, already aware that he had no way to do anything inside this domain he found himself in. He can die at any moment because he is too weak to do anything.
His heavenly sword energy is useless, and he can feel that. So since he had already lost, he might as well make sure he wasn’t sent away in the most agonizing way possible.
"I suppose I have lost, huh?"
"That is only natural, kid. You have proven yourself to everyone. I, for one, am impressed, and that should go a long way, kid. I am not easily impressed."
Jest smiled and nodded. "I suppose clearing four floors is okay for now. I won the 4th level by luck, so there is that. However, before I leave, can you answer some questions for me?"
"Go on, kid. You have earned an answer or two."
Jest gave him a gentle smile, and then he asked the question, "I can see your sword realm has the fire attribute. Does this have something to do with your sword path or your elemental affinity?"

"Both," Sword Divine Yuan answered. "I am a flame human, so naturally I have an affinity for the flame element. However, my sword path is also flame-based, since the fire element is again natural to me.
However, if you are wondering if you can learn other elemental affinities and incorporate them into your sword realm, then my only answer will be no."
"Can I know why?"

"Incorporating an element into your sword realm is something that can be accomplished if your understanding of the element is strong enough. However, here lies the case where your sword path is not aligned with your elemental affinity.
This means you have no way of incorporating that element into the sword realm. Of course, you can learn it and perhaps find a way to use it. However, that would take just too much time.

Take the Sword Sea you had just witnessed. If the owner had time and patience, they could learn the water element and, from the Sword Emperor stage to the Sword Legend stage, use it to shape their sword realm.
Trust me, with the nature of his sword realm, adding water to it will make it something to be feared greatly.
The same can be said for the broken sword realm. If the owner were to add the metal element, there is no telling what could become of it.
But to accomplish this, one would have to have patience because, trust me, when it comes to creating an element-based sword realm, there is nothing more daunting and taxing.
But it all borders on their sword path. Would augmenting their sword realm in the long run align or deviate from their sword path?"
"That is a lot to take in," Jest exhales and lets his mind free up some space. He had learned a lot from the small sword Divine Yuan mentioned.

If there is one thing he has learned thus far, it is the ability to be patient in all things. He is someone walking his own path, so there is no telling just what he can accomplish if he has the patience.
But there is also the question of whether he can handle what he has heard. He is not in a rush to become a Sword Emperor or even form his sword realm.
If possible, just like how he wasted 120 years learning all 1.6 million sword moves, he can waste his time and learn an element and incorporate it into his sword path before forming a sword realm.
"You know, one good thing about walking my own path is the flexibility to do as I please. I can choose to learn as many elements as I want and incorporate as many as I can before advancing,"
Sword Divine Yuan smiles. "That is indeed true. You have the luxury to do any crazy thing you want. However, as you ask, would that align with what you want to achieve?"
Jest smiled and gave Sword Divine Yuan a wink. "That is the thing, senior. My sword path has no defined path. Basically, I can just go any direction I want, and it would be fine.
So I can choose to learn the flame element and incorporate it into my sword path without any issues. You can say my sword path is formless. It can take any form I want."

Sword Divine Yuan shook his head in disbelief. There is just no way to describe what kind of monster Jest is. From the start of his journey on the sword bridge, it had been one shocking event after another.
"I suppose all I can do is wish you the best and hope you succeed. If one day you become a Sword Divine, you can come challenge me again. Maybe we will have a good duel.
For now, you are not qualified to challenge me, since you wouldn’t even know when you die."
"I understand, and I promise to give you a good fight the next time we meet." Jest ended with his classic smile. His body was engulfed in flames, and before he could blink, only ash remained.
The next second, Jest appeared in front of the sword bridge, which is actually a tall pagoda.
"It really should be called sword pagoda," Jest joked.
Then he turned to face the two Immortal Lords looking at him.
"Elder Ritsu and Elder Willa, I hope with how dangerous you are looking at me, you aren’t trying to renege on our deal, you know, allowing me to challenge that brat to a deathmatch."
The kid who threatened to make him his slave sure had to die, and so, despite becoming a star in the Whispering Wind Sword Sect, he still wanted him dead.

Elder Ritsu, who is the acting sect leader, snapped out of his daze and answered, "You are now an Inner Disciple, so you have to wait till that kid becomes an Inner Disciple before you can challenge him."
"Immortal Lord Ritsu is right," Elder Willa stepped in. "For now, you must come with us. We have been instructed to send you to a special place where you will be staying for now."
"How convenient. I guess I will find another way to take his head off his body," Jest muttered, and then started following the two Immortal Lords.

chapters.title: Chapter 1378: Purple Sword Garden
paragraphs: As Jest and the two elders moved through the sect, many disciples who had recognized him from the just-ended sword bridge challenge looked at him with all kinds of emotions.
There was reverence, respect, envy, jealousy, and the one that would make anyone in Jest’s place cringe: affection.
Most of said emotion is coming from the ladies, but in a very cringe way, considering the kind of thoughts running through their heads while they think this.
Regardless, Jest had become a hot cake, as shown by how everyone was looking at him, including the elders.
There is a big chance he might succeed in walking his own path. If that were to happen, they all know he would become a great help.

So while many were initially dissatisfied with him because he was a no-name who was allowed to challenge the sword bridge, seeing what he has accomplished and what he is likely to accomplish in the future, they all want to leave a good impression.
If only they knew, Jest mainly wanted to open the door for everyone, regardless of whether they liked him.
Of course, there are those who hate him for real, and so no matter what kind of genius he is, they would never show him the respect he deserves.𝙛𝓻𝒆𝒆𝒘𝙚𝓫𝙣𝙤𝒗𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
"I hope you are not taking me somewhere to make me disappear," Jest asked, flying behind Immortal Lord Ritsu and Willa.
Elder Willa turned and looked at him. "Getting rid of you is as simple as snapping my finger, so rest assured, we have no plans on killing you."

"Happy to hear that," Jest smiled, admiring the space around him. "This place is not half bad. I am sure in a couple of years, when I become a Sword Emperor or Divine, I will use my influence to attract investors to come make it more beautiful."
The two Immortal Lords ignored him. To them, Jest is now an asset, so allowing him to mess around is a good thing.
"I have a question."
"Ask."
"Can I decide to decline my status as an Inner Disciple and go back to being an Outer Disciple?"
Elder Ritsu turned and gave him the same look Elder Willa gave him. "Does this have something to do with that kid you wanted to challenge to the deathmatch?"
"Maybe, maybe not," Jest smiled.

"You cannot do that. But even if you could, I wouldn’t have allowed it. You have so much talent that, if nurtured well, will one day put you on the map of the universe, so allowing a petty misunderstanding to come in the way of that is just stupid.

Also, while the sect can indeed protect you while you are here, as a disciple, you are required to go out for missions, so killing someone whose father is an Immortal Lord with several other powerful cultivators on his retainer is just being stupid."
"Ha," Jest smiled. "So in your opinion, I shouldn’t kill him because his father is not someone I can afford to offend,"
"That is exactly what I meant,"
Jest shook his head, a wave of hate emitting from his body. "Elder Ritsu, have you ever been a slave?"
"I can’t say I was unfortunate to be one,"

"Then you should know that being asked to work 12 hours a day with only 3 hours of rest is not something to be happy about. The day my mother gave birth to me, she was forced to go deep into a cave, and that was the last time she was heard from.
I started carrying an axe and a hoe from the age of six, and for the better part of my life, I only knew the pained smile of slaves.
It doesn’t matter how hurt you are; when your shift comes, you are required to go and work, for that is the purpose and the life of a slave.
To them, a slave is an expendable tool. They can always get more slaves, so a few deaths are nothing to worry about.
So imagine how it feels if a brat dares to say my life’s worth is to be his slave. It is painful, Elder Ritsu, and for that, I will kill him.
I don’t care who his family is or what they are capable of. I will kill him, and there is nothing anyone can do to stop me."
Elder Ritsu and Willa were left with nothing to even say. They clearly understood what Jest meant, and that was enough for them to know where his stubbornness to kill that brat was coming from.
There was nothing they could do to stop him, for they knew his hatred was coming from deep within his soul. Such hatred cannot be stopped.
However, knowing the kind of asset Jest is, there was just something about protecting him from himself.
If he were to become a problem now, then he would one day become a pain in the ass or be killed before he could make a name for himself.
’I guess we will just keep him engaged long enough to find a permanent solution for him. Either way, he cannot be allowed to kill that madman’s son.’
After a few minutes of flight, they appeared before a garden filled mostly with purple-leaved plants. At a distance, Jest could sense some natural sword-like energy emitting from the garden.
If he didn’t know better, he would say the plants were swords. However, as they drew closer, that thought started to change.
"What is this place?"
"This is the Purple Sword Garden."
"I can see that, Elder Ritsu. I meant to ask, what is this garden made of?"

Elder Ritsu paused for a moment and then said, "A very long time ago, a sword immortal on the verge of ascending to the rank of a sword god lost control of his sword domain while comprehending sword will, and so he died.
However, before dying, he used every last understanding of the sword he had gathered over the years to transform his domain, manifesting it as a garden.

There are many theories as to why his sword domain could still live while he was dead, but the most logical one, of course, was that in his last moment, he was able to comprehend sword will, and that will is what is keeping this garden alive."

Jest remained calm on the outside, but on the inside, his heart was beating like a drum. That was because, from where he stood now, all he could see were billions of swords transformed into one big and beautiful garden.
"Impressive," he couldn’t help muttering.
"If I were to cultivate here for just a year, I would be able to expand my understanding of the sword by several degrees. There is just so much to learn from this garden,"
Elder Ritsu and Willa smiled.

It seemed keeping him engaged wouldn’t be too hard after all. Someone like Jest is a curious being. He would not stop expanding his understanding of the sword, provided he had something to learn from.
The Purple Sword Garden now seemed like the best place for him to start. After all, many thirsted for this opportunity due to its many benefits.
They stopped in front of the garden.
"This is as far as we can take you. You are on your own now."
Jest thanked them and quickly entered the garden, eager to learn...

I started carrying an axe and a hoe from the age of six, and for the better part of my life, I only knew the pained smile of slaves.
It doesn’t matter how hurt you are; when your shift comes, you are required to go and work, for that is the purpose and the life of a slave.
To them, a slave is an expendable tool.
They can always get more slaves, so a few deaths are nothing to worry about.
So imagine how it feels if a brat dares to say my life’s worth is to be his slave.
It is painful, Elder Ritsu, and for that, I will kill him.
I don’t care who his family is or what they are capable of.
I will kill him, and there is nothing anyone can do to stop me."
Elder Ritsu and Willa were left with nothing to even say.
They clearly understood what Jest meant, and that was enough for them to know where his stubbornness to kill that brat was coming from.
There was nothing they could do to stop him, for they knew his hatred was coming from deep within his soul.
Such hatred cannot be stopped.
However, knowing the kind of asset Jest is, there was just something about protecting him from himself.
If he were to become a problem now, then he would one day become a pain in the ass or be killed before he could make a name for himself.
’I guess we will just keep him engaged long enough to find a permanent solution for him.
Either way, he cannot be allowed to kill that madman’s son.’
After a few minutes of flight, they appeared before a garden filled mostly with purple-leaved plants.
At a distance, Jest could sense some natural sword-like energy emitting from the garden.
If he didn’t know better, he would say the plants were swords.
However, as they drew closer, that thought started to change.
"What is this place?"
"This is the Purple Sword Garden."
"I can see that, Elder Ritsu.
I meant to ask, what is this garden made of?"

Elder Ritsu paused for a moment and then said, "A very long time ago, a sword immortal on the verge of ascending to the rank of a sword god lost control of his sword domain while comprehending sword will, and so he died.
However, before dying, he used every last understanding of the sword he had gathered over the years to transform his domain, manifesting it as a garden.

There are many theories as to why his sword domain could still live while he was dead, but the most logical one, of course, was that in his last moment, he was able to comprehend sword will, and that will is what is keeping this garden alive."
Jest remained calm on the outside, but on the inside, his heart was beating like a drum.
That was because, from where he stood now, all he could see were billions of swords transformed into one big and beautiful garden.
"Impressive," he couldn’t help muttering.
"If I were to cultivate here for just a year, I would be able to expand my understanding of the sword by several degrees.
There is just so much to learn from this garden,"
Elder Ritsu and Willa smiled.
It seemed keeping him engaged wouldn’t be too hard after all.
Someone like Jest is a curious being.
He would not stop expanding his understanding of the sword, provided he had something to learn from.
The Purple Sword Garden now seemed like the best place for him to start.
After all, many thirsted for this opportunity due to its many benefits.
They stopped in front of the garden.
"This is as far as we can take you.
You are on your own now."
Jest thanked them and quickly entered the garden, eager to learn...

chapters.title: Chapter 1379: Inaya
paragraphs: The moment Jest stepped into the purple sword garden, his sword intent activated on its own, instantly filling the air.
However, instead of him feeling his surroundings thanks to his sword intent, he felt like he was swimming inside a pool of sword energy.
The sword intent inside the garden felt like it had taken hold of the entire garden, rewriting everything within it.
"Fascinating. So one day, I would be able to influence the very laws within a space using my sword Realm ."
The sword intent in the air, from what Jest could feel, had overridden the laws of the garden, making it so that once he enters there, the only thing he can do is train his sword intent.
Jest didn’t mind that, for he had already expected that even before he entered the garden.
"The air is filled with sword intent to the point that merely breathing is allowing me to understand some mysteries of the sword."
As someone who had mastered the foundation of swordsmanship completely, he could sense that breathing inside this garden was not so simple.
There was so much to it that he just could not place his finger on it.
"Let me find a place to sit and get absorbed into this. The faster I become stronger, the quicker I can sever that bastard’s head off his neck."
A pale smile appeared on his face as he moved deeper into the forest.

On the outside, Elder Ritsu and Willa stood there for a few minutes, unblinking. It was as if they were waiting for something to happen. However, even after five minutes had passed and nothing had happened, they took a deep breath.
"I guess we have nothing to worry about then," Elder Ritsu said, a bit relieved.
"It seems so. For now, we should leave before it is too late for us."
The two elders left, not even turning to look back. They can play the ’we weren’t aware card if something were to happen later.’

Meanwhile, inside the garden, Jest slowly moved deeper, paying attention to the changes around him. The closer he got to the inner layer of the garden, the deeper his connection to the sword intent in the air became.
This also seemed to boost his understanding of the sword intent.
Suddenly, he came to a stop when he sensed danger coming from behind. He turned his head to the left just fast enough for a deadly thin sword to zip past his head.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
He used the movement of his head to move further to his left before he turned. The face that greeted him was that of a lady whose gaze burned with the desire to kill.
"Let me guess, you were cultivating here, and so when you sense my presence, you felt disturbed and now want to kill me," Jest said, pulling out his sword.
The lady was a Sword Emperor, but he wasn’t afraid.
"Who are you and what are you doing here?" the lady asked, but Jest merely scoffed and turned toward his left...
"One thing I hate is a coward. If you are going to face me, then at least have the decency to face me in your real body. Why hide behind a clone to try to intimidate me?"
There are many things that can be understood if one’s senses aren’t strong enough. One of said things is the ability to see through illusions or clones.
In this case, Jest, who had already faced so many dangers, sensed the lady who attacked him was no Sword Emperor. In fact, she wasn’t even a real person.
This could only mean she was a clone.
However, while being a clone sounded so simple, Jest could tell there was more to it. But he wasn’t in the mood to entertain her.
He did not know how long he had before he would be taken out of the purple sword garden, so he wasn’t about to entertain anyone who would distract him from what he was after.
This was why he went straight to the point without any hesitation.
His words hung in the air for a few minutes before the space warped, and a green-haired lady walked out, wearing an amused smile on her lips.
When Jest’s gaze landed on her, a sigh escaped his lips. "Ah, my bad luck."
The lady now staring at him was someone he recognised all too well.
After being chased down for almost a year, nearly dying a few times, he finally managed to corner Seraphina.

However, before he could kill her, this lady appeared and saved her. While it was merely her consciousness that came to her rescue, Jest captured her face so he would never come anywhere close to her ever again.
Now, she stood before him as an Immortal Lord and a sword Immortal. His luck couldn’t be any worse than that.
"Small world, huh?" the lady said before she waved off the clone. It turned into sword Qi and flew back into her body.
Jest remained standing, his expression calm, but inwardly, he was freaking out like hell. ’Upon all the sects I could have gone to, why did I end up in one she is in?’

Right now, he had no idea if this lady planned on killing him or not. When they first met, it was he who was about to kill someone under her protection. Now, it seemed he was the one who needed saving.
His swordsmanship wasn’t enough to do anything, so he could only stare at the lady. A few minutes later, he smiled. "Small world indeed."
He let the air pass on his words before adding, "I am Jest, by the way."
"You can call me Inaya."
"Inaya. Can’t say I have heard such a beautiful name before." Since he couldn’t save his own skin, he might as well suck up to her and hope she had mercy on him.
The smile on Inaya’s face was just too beautiful not to mean anything. In fact, she looked like someone who had seen suitable prey and was about to devour it.
"Your name also has a peculiar sound to it. I have never met anyone named Jest."
Jest smiled. "I get that a lot."
Inaya nodded, then the smile on her face vanished. "So tell me, Jest, how do you want to do it?"
Jest’s heartbeat jumped, almost bursting out from his chest. "Do what, please?" he asked, already prepared to die at any moment.

Inaya looked at him for a few seconds, then she spoke. "You are now a disciple in my sect, so naturally, you need my permission to cultivate inside this garden. So tell me, how do you want to go about that?"
Haaaaa.
Jest exhaled. ’I swear, one day I will teach this bitch a lesson.’ Just now, he thought he was at death’s door.
"If Sect Leader Inaya is using this place, then I would politely excuse myself so I do not disturb her." Jest was about to turn and leave when Inaya moved and appeared before him.
She grabbed his hand, and before he could do anything, they had moved several kilometers deeper into the garden.
A few seconds later, they appeared before a small pool.

chapters.title: Chapter 1380: She Is Wicked
paragraphs: There was nothing strange about the pool.
It was just a small pond filled with clean water.
However, despite its ordinary nature, Jest couldn’t help feeling like there was something terribly wrong with the water in the pool.
The longer he stared at it, the deeper the weirdness kept settling in his mind.

Inaya let go of his hand and pointed at the pool. "What you are looking at is sword qi transformed into a pool. Naturally, it is real water; however, it is contained inside a single strand of Sword God Energy.
If I can get my hands on that sword energy, wouldn’t it be nice?" she asked, the same smile appearing on her face.
"It would indeed be awesome."
"In that case, wouldn’t it be great if you could help me look for it? I mean, it would be nice to help a senior, right?"
Jest smiled and nodded.

"Wonderful. It might take you at least a hundred years to find it, so once you accomplish it, you can go back to training here for as long as you want. I wouldn’t disturb you. As for our previous meeting, you can forget it ever happened."
Jest turned and looked at her with a serious expression. "Just like that?" he asked, and she nodded.
"Very simple and easy, right?"
"Very easy indeed," Jest smirked, a look of satisfaction appearing on his face. He took a few steps toward the pool.

Jest knew she had plans for him the moment she chose not to attack him. However, instead of making it seem like she needed his help, she tried to make it seem like forgiving him and allowing him to use the purple sword garden was a privilege she would be granting him.
But Jest didn’t mind that one bit. In his head, he had already won. Spending a hundred years helping her so he could spend a lifetime training was not a bad deal at all.

"You know, in this life, there are those destined to suffer and those fated to have bad luck." Jest turned and looked at Inaya. "I am both of those things. But I am also someone fated to have all the good things in this life."
Inaya said nothing, but she could sense a deeper meaning in what Jest was saying.
She waited for Jest to continue...
"My bad luck is meeting you twice, knowing full well you are a wicked person."
Inaya grinned. "That is not a nice word to say to a lady, Jest."

"But it is true, though. You are wicked. You are an Immortal Lord, probably several thousand years old. To you, a hundred years is nothing. However, I need those hundred years to advance my understanding of the sword and also my cultivation base.
So asking me to spend that long to look for something I may never find is just being wicked."

"One hundred years is the minimum. This means that until you find it, you can never leave this pool. And as you said, one hundred years is nothing to me. So, guess how long I can guard this place just so I can keep you here?"
Jest gave her a small smile before extending his hand toward the sword pool. "I may have bad luck, but I also have good luck."
The water rippled and suddenly surged. Then, from deep within the pool, a thin sword flashed out and zipped through the air a few times before coming to a stop in front of Jest.

Inaya’s eyes widened at the sight. The sword was made of golden sword qi. However, the energy it contained was one thing Jest was most afraid of. Still, to show off and aura farm, he let it hover before him.
"H-How?" She tried to ask a question, but her words couldn’t come out.
"I believe this is what you are looking for." Jest made the sword move toward her. When he was sure she had what she wanted, he took off from there.
"Don’t disturb me again, wicked lady." He vanished from sight, leaving Inaya wondering just what had happened. Jest was supposed to spend at least one hundred years inside the pool.
However, with a casual wave of his hand, the condensed God Sword Energy appeared. That was just not possible, and she could tell that.
However, now that she had the sword energy before her, something she had been searching for for over three hundred thousand years already, she just couldn’t think straight.
By the time she managed to calm her heart down and make sense of what had happened, Jest was long gone. An hour had already passed.
"I promised to let him stay here, so I guess I will cut him some slack." She smiled, then vanished from sight, appearing somewhere far from the purple sword garden.
Now that she had the God Sword Energy, the next thing to do was refine and absorb it, which would take so much time, so Jest was safe to remain inside the garden for as long as he wanted.
Years went by in the blink of an eye.

Jest remained in the garden for 120 years before coming out. He had learned so much that, the moment he came out, he decided to challenge the Sword Emperors in the sect and copy their sword realms so he could form his own.
It took another ten years, but he managed to form his sword realm.
He named it the Genesis Sword Realm, one of the most dangerous sword realms anyone had ever seen. The moment his sword realm was formed, he became undisputed.𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖
As a Sword Emperor, he qualified to become a core disciple, so he took the exams and passed with flying colors.
He was later sent out to the outside world to gain some experience. Jest spent fifty years roaming from one planet to another, challenging anyone he wanted.
He made so many enemies, but he also gained friends.
Three hundred years after he returned to the sect, he became a Sword Divine. It could be considered a sudden leap, considering it takes many thousands of years to become Sword Divines.
However, he accomplished that. Naturally, the moment he became a Sword Divine, his name spread everywhere. He became an overnight sensation, a name that brought out all kinds of emotions.

This was because, on the day he became a Sword Divine, a tablet appeared, followed by a declaration. Inside the declaration, it was said that the Sword Dao had recognised Jest as someone who had accomplished a great feat, and as such, he had been recognised.
This declaration prompted many to seek him out.

Because of this, Jest had to leave the sect because staying there wasn’t safe for him. However, before leaving, he first fulfilled his promise and killed the brat who claimed he was good at being his slave.
Two hundred years after Jest left, another name appeared on the Sword Dao tablet. Inaya became the second person to be recognised by the Sword Dao.

When she found out what had happened, she also left and decided to search for Jest. Five hundred years later, they met again. Jest had just become a Sword Legend, while she was on the verge of ascending to godhood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1381: Sword Knowledge
paragraphs: Kent opened his eyes, only for a powerful wave of heavenly sword energy to explode out of him. In an instant, his entire body felt like he had been recreated using nothing but sword energy.
His sword intent rose from Level 6 to Level 7 and continued to increase rapidly. The same thing was also happening to his sword aura.
Soon, he reached level 8 but kept climbing.
Basically, his entire understanding of his sword realm was being shaped by what he had learned from Jest’s memories.
The memory ended when he and Inaya met again.

However, before that, Jest went through a lot. First was his training in the Purple Sword Garden. The time he spent there took his sword intent from Level 5 to Level 9. The same was true for his sword Qi/aura.

After he had reached that stage, he knew he had to form his sword realm and finally become a sword emperor. So he left, and with his popularity that was earned thanks to what he had achieved on the sword bridge, he managed to learn five more sword realms.
Ten years later, he formed his own.

Initially, he wanted to follow the path that Divine Collins had told him about. However, he realised he had more time to later shape his sword realm with any element he wanted, so he formed the sword realm by comprehending every last aspect of the 1.6 million sword moves he had learned.
He had already mastered them, but he sat down and examined each move, making sense of every small thing about it. He went through all 1.6 million sword moves.
Once he was satisfied, he formed the Genesis sword realm, the same sword realm that went on to become the Genesis Sword Domain.
When he formed his sword realm, it was basic.
Unlike many realms that manifest crazy stiff, the only thing that changed when he activated his sword realm was the direction of the wind.
Initially, many laughed at him, some even claiming his journey ended there. However, after tasting what he had accomplished, they all gave him the respect he deserved.
But he went beyond that.
He took the conceptualisation of his sword realm to the next level of crazy. He first comprehended the wind element, which he mastered in just five years.
Once he did that, he merged it with his sword realm. That merge gave him all the boost he needed as a swordsman.
The wind element made it so that he could move at a speed so fast that when his sword realm was activated, even the fastest True Immortal would struggle to catch up to him.
However, Jest wasn’t satisfied, so he learned the lightning element. This gave the Genesis Sword Realm the boost in combat power it needed.
Yet again, he went further, and by the time he neared the Sword Divine stage, he had added ice and fire to it as well.
When he became a Sword Divine, he added the metal element, making it the final element he added to his sword realm.
The day he became a Sword Divine, he challenged the sword bridge again and won the fifth level within ten minutes.
Sword Divine Collins tried his best, but he failed miserably. He tried to challenge the sixth level, but facing a Sword Legend was different. Even so, he lasted two hours before he ran out of energy.

That battle made him aware of his limitations, and so he entered seclusion after he left the sect, and for years, he shaped his understanding of the sword and his elements to the point that if he were to face the sixth-level Sword Legend, he would win after a few minutes.
But because he was on the run, he had to give up that idea and embark on one adventure after another. He had plans to return one day to challenge the 6th level.
In the end, he became a Sword Legend himself. By then, he had become a True Immortal.
Everybody wanted a piece of him because his name appearing on the sword dao tablet meant he
knew something many did not.
Thankfully, after Inaya absorbed the sword god energy, she gained so much that the sword dao gave her some of the recognition, taking a few loads off Jest’s.
This allowed him to move around and further strengthen his understanding of his swordsmanship.
The day they met, he was about to enter seclusion and try to reach the Immortal King stage, since he had already formed over seven Immortal Qis.
Kent had no idea what happened next, but he was sure the reason why he hated Inaya had to do with what she did next. Too bad the memory ended before he could see that.
Ten days later, he opened his eyes, a wave of sharp sword intent oozing out from them. His sword gaze had undergone some changes, and that could be seen from the air around him.
Kent quickly checked the messages that had appeared before him. A few seconds later, he looked away and stared at the pagoda in the distance.
He also had the sword bridge inside the sword tower. However, he knew the swordsmen on each floor would be different from the ones Jest’s faced.
Even so, he had to conquer the first six floors, which meant he had to defeat a sword legend while he had no sword realm.
In the memories he had seen, Jest defeated many sword legends and even a few sword immortals. However, that was possible because of his Genesis Sword Realm.
Kent had yet to meet two more requirements before his sword realm would awaken.
He had yet to conquer the first six levels of the sword bridge in this life.

The other requirement was, of course, conquering the sword legend on the sixth level of the sword bridge. This must be accomplished by Jest, meaning he must review memories of that before his sword realm would awaken.
The tower gave him these requirements, so he was sure Jest would do that. This meant he would have to review more of his memories and know what happened next.
This meant he must go see Inaya, for she was the key to everything. If he wants to awaken his sword realm, he must go back home.

As for the first six levels of the sword bridge inside the tower, Kent stood up and flew toward it. He might not have a sword realm yet, but he had copied thousands of sword realms over the years he spent on the move.
And while he had yet to awaken the Divine sword aura and intent, he had knowledge of how to fight sword legends and even sword immortals.

Even better, he had the many sword skills and techniques that Jest had created over the years, now at his disposal. Basically, he was now loaded with so much knowledge about his sword path than he was weeks ago.
The best part was that he could now shape his sword path and correct the mistakes he had made before. He could make sure that this time, not a single mistake would go unfixed.

He might have reached the ranks of Swordsmanship, but that didn’t mean he hadn’t made any mistakes. He had made a whole lot of mistakes, and now, with the second chance he had, he planned on walking a flawless path.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
But before that, he had to first clear the sword bridge to the sixth level.

chapters.title: Chapter 1382: Making His Decision
paragraphs: [Sword Bridge - 6th Level]
Kent stood still, his expression calm as he stared at the 6th swordsman he was about to fight.
"Tower, why is he just a Sword Emperor?"
Kent asked, his tone sounding a bit dissatisfied.
It had only been an hour since he entered the sword bridge. However, in these few minutes, he cleared five levels like they were nothing to him.
Obviously, for someone who had knowledge of swordsmanship to the peak of the Sword Legend stage, he surely had some form of superiority against those below that stage.
That was why, when the first level of the sword bridge gave him a Sword King, he became bored instantly. But it didn’t stop there; the next two levels were also Sword Kings.
He ended those battles within five minutes.

When he got to the 4th level, the challenger was a Sword Emperor, and so was the 5th level. Now, it seemed he would be facing a Sword Emperor again on the 6th level, and to him, that just didn’t make any sense.
From Jest’s memories, only the first level was a Sword King. The second, third, and fourth were Sword Emperors, with the 5th level being a Sword Divine and the 6th being a Sword Legend.
But he wasn’t getting the same treatment here.
[The master should know the sword bridge examines the master’s swordsmanship level and assigns a suitable challenge for him.]
"So you are saying that because I am a Sword King, the sword bridge decided to scale the challengers to my level."
[The master is overqualified, but that is how it is, so the master must not be too disappointed.]
Kent smirked, disappointed.

The sword bridge that Jest challenged featured real people as the challengers, but even they couldn’t speak. While their swordsmanship is perfect, it isn’t the same as facing a target that can talk and express their emotions.
There is just not that thrill, and so, in the end, Kent defeated the 6th-level Sword Emperor within five moves. The moment he handled that, he stopped climbing the levels.

What he wanted wasn’t what he got, so there was no need for him to even continue climbing it. If by chance he managed to one day go back to the Whispering Wind Sword Sect, he would challenge that sword bridge.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎

But while he was left disappointed, the requirement for him to awaken his sword realm had also been completed. The only thing left was for Jest to challenge the sword bridge again and defeat the 6th-level Sword Legend.
The moment that happened, his sword realm would awaken, and he would finally advance to the Sword Emperor stage.
He had already met both requirements to become a Sword Emperor. The only thing holding him back now was his sword realm.

"This is a bit complicated. While I have no plans to keep myself occupied for now, becoming a Sword Emperor is now a must. I will need my sword realm for the mission I will soon be going on, so I must become a Sword Emperor and, if possible, even a Sword Divine." He took a deep breath, then he smiled.
"However, I must first meet Inaya and find out what happened between us. While I hate to see her again, what I have remembered so far doesn’t justify my reluctance to meet her.
There must be something extremely wrong with why I don’t want to meet her."
Kent smirked, feeling a bit silly.
Finding out that Inaya was the one who prevented him from killing Seraphina wasn’t too much to take in. She was a sword immortal and an Immortal Lord, so that was perfectly normal.
However, what he never saw coming was her becoming the second name on the Sword Dao Tablet.

That was a surprise. He didn’t know what happened after she refined the sword god energy and absorbed it, but he knew her name appearing on the Sword Dao Tablet must have something to do with what she had gained after absorbing it.
"When Vexthra told me to go to her, she said Inaya had been looking for me for years. She even mentioned that she is a Sword Supreme.
If that is the case, then why hasn’t she become a Sword Celestial when her name is clearly on the Sword Dao Tablet?"
Kent suddenly felt his back break into a cold sweat.
At once, he felt like he had done something to her that, over the years, had prevented her from becoming a Sword Celestial.
"Maybe I am overthinking things. Maybe she is just not ready to take that step yet."
Even after convincing himself, he still couldn’t place his finger on the idea that he was, in a way, involved.
"This means I must meet her, and according to Vexthra, Gaia said she is on Planet Brymrr." Kent paused and smiled slightly. "Looks like I have to go back home."
From what Kent had gathered, Planet Brymrr is a unique world. This means there may be gods and even Supremes there. This also means Inaya would be at full strength when they met.
This also means she would be able to do anything she wanted to Kent without him being able to say otherwise.
"Tower, I am cooked, aren’t I?"
[The master should already be aware of the dangers in a Unique World, so he must prepare accordingly.]

"Oh, please, you and I both know there is no planning for this. I will be walking into the maw of sharks. The only consolation prize here is I know deep within me that Inaya won’t kill me. But she is wicked, so hurting me is not out of the picture."
[Then the master is indeed cooked and roasted.]
Kent chuckled. There was just nothing that he could do to avoid seeing Inaya. She would be happy to see him for sure, but did that mean he would be happy to see her?
"Tower, sometimes it seems the universe just wants to conspire against me for her amusement."
[The master is overthinking.]
"Of course you will support her. I mean, you are a cosmic entity yourself, so the bias is plain as day."
[I am on the master’s side always. My loyalty is to the master and will always be with the master.]
"I know that, and sorry if my words questioned your loyalty."
[The master shouldn’t worry. I perfectly understood what the master was trying to say.]
Kent nodded and then reached into his tower storage and retrieved two more Memory Keys.
These ones belonged to the next incarnation he had once lived: The Ruthless Bandit.
From what he knew, he was the master of the Night Riders. Uncle Drew and the others tried to hide that from him, but he was too smart.
However, as to why they decided not to say anything, he planned to find out soon.
"Tower, what are my wives up to?"

[Goddess Vexthra is still inside Lady Unity’s Love Space with Lady Dia, Selene, and Elaine. However, the legion and the rest of your wives are almost done searching for the clues left on the 7th floor of the dungeon.]
"So they will soon be heading to the 8th floor."
[Yes, master.]
"Good. Inform them to wait for me."
[As you say, master.]
Kent nodded and activated the Memory Key. The next second, his consciousness was somewhere else.

chapters.title: Chapter 1383: Lex Morvane
paragraphs: Kent appeared in front of a tall tower stretching as far as the eye could see. It is extremely tall and lined with several windows, showing that there are many rooms in the tower.
He stood there for a few seconds, admiring the structure.
It seemed to be made from limestone or jade that looked like limestone. Either way, it was tall, beautiful, and a bit strange.
The strangeness was due to the smoke coming from a window in what appeared to be the sixth floor. Kent narrowed his eyes at this window and even tried to use his soul map to see who was inside.
It was the only window that was open.

However, no matter how hard he tried, he just couldn’t see inside. So he decided to enter and look for himself. He entered, and, as he expected, the interior was indeed lavish, showing that the owner of this tower was rather rich.
He made his way up the stairway, and soon he was standing in front of the door to the room whose window he had seen open when he was outside.
"Come in."
Before he could knock, a voice came from inside, telling him to enter. Kent opened the door, and the first thing he saw was the back of a young man sitting before the window, smoking a pipe.

He had lush silver hair that was only a bit too tall to be called short. He was clad in royal wear, showing he was royalty. However, around him, Kent could not see any aura that suggested he was an Immortal, God, Supreme, or even Celestial.
"You are finally here," the young man said before slowly turning to face Kent.

When their gazes met, Kent felt like he had known this person for a lifetime. However, this feeling also came with a wave of sadness and anger, the kind that would turn the most innocent into a monster.
"You are the Ruthless Bandit," Kent asked, his eyes narrowing a bit.
The young man pulled the pipe away from his lips and let the smoke come from the corners of his mouth before a small smile appeared on his face.
"I was called that many years ago." He stood up, walked toward a chair, and sat down. He gestured for Kent to sit down as well. "You can call me Lex Morvane."
"I am Kent Madson."

There was just something about the way the young man was handling their meeting that kept giving Kent the creeps. He was too polite, and on top of that, he seemed to be testing Kent in ways he didn’t even know.
"So why are you here, Kent?"

Kent narrowed his eyes, hearing this obvious question. "Well, genius, you happen to be my incarnation, and so in my attempt to remember this life, I found myself here, so maybe cut the act and get on to helping me get what I came here for. I am on the clock here."
Lex looked at Kent for a few seconds before a smirk appeared on his face. "I see. So you want to know about this life, huh?"
"Yes. That is what I literally said."
"Oh, I see." Lex turned toward a bookshelf and picked up a book. He brushed the dust off it and turned to Kent.

"Are you really sure you want to know about this life? I mean, it wasn’t our best life, and while I would like you to know the horrors of the universe this early, when it comes to my life, you would learn that even the purest flower is more lethal than the most potent poison."
Kent didn’t say anything for a few seconds. He first let Lex’s words settle in his mind for a few minutes before he nodded.
"I want to. If I don’t know, then when would be the right time to do it?"

"If you say so. But be aware that whatever you will be reading in this book will affect you in ways you cannot bring yourself to take for granted. If you, in any way, feel like you can’t handle it, just close it and store it somewhere you will not be compelled to read it.
Once you recover and you feel like you can handle it one more time, then you can go for it."

Kent nodded, a bit taken aback by how Lex was handling everything. In his mind, he would be meeting a ruthless person on a bloody battlefield, clad in tattered armor with blood covering most of his armor and even his face.
However, Lex looked like someone who had undergone therapy and had now turned a new Chapter in his life, one in which he strove to maintain the peace he sought.
This only made Kent wonder just what kind of life he had lived that had turned him into such a person. It wasn’t normal, and that was plain as day now that he thought about it.
"Here you go," Lex handed the book over to Kent. On the cover, he saw the book’s title, which darkened his expression.
"Birth of Evil: Tale of the Ruthless Bandit. Vol. 1"
The title of the book was just something he knew would contain some of the most horrifying experiences he would go through.
He already saw how Elina died during the Primordial Era and how it affected Chaos. He also saw his life as a slave who had to endure the worst kind of torture from the day he learned to walk.
As for his life as the Faceless Assassin, he saw the lengths his mother had to go through to protect him from assassins.
But despite all those unfortunate experiences, he wouldn’t classify his life during those times as evil. So for the Ruthless Bandit’s name to be branded as one, he knew things were about to get real.
"Remember, when it gets a bit overwhelming, just close the book and rest for a while."
Kent nodded and stored the book away. He then looked at Lex for a few minutes before asking to leave.
"I will wait for you to come for the other volumes. However, don’t be pressured to come, since I have nowhere else to be."
Kent nodded. A second later, he woke up inside the tower. He quickly reached into the tower storage and pulled out the book.
This one was much bigger than the memory diaries. Without even opening it, Kent knew he would be reading a story instead of diary entries.
"Should I dig in right away, or should I give it a few more days to do that? I literally have more time on my hands now that I am not moving toward the edge of the galaxy."
Kent looked at the book for a few seconds before deciding to open it and see what was inside.
Flipping to the first page, he only saw a few lines of text...
"This is the account of a beautiful life twisted by the evil of men—the tale of the one who embodied evil in all forms and essence. Life of Lex Morvane, the Ruthless Bandit."
Kent took a deep breath, letting his mind clear. He wanted to see what happened next, so he needed his mind settled before diving in.
A few seconds later, he turned to page two.

sentences.text: Kent appeared in front of a tall tower stretching as far as the eye could see.
It is extremely tall and lined with several windows, showing that there are many rooms in the tower.
He stood there for a few seconds, admiring the structure.
It seemed to be made from limestone or jade that looked like limestone.
Either way, it was tall, beautiful, and a bit strange.
The strangeness was due to the smoke coming from a window in what appeared to be the sixth floor.
Kent narrowed his eyes at this window and even tried to use his soul map to see who was inside.
It was the only window that was open.
However, no matter how hard he tried, he just couldn’t see inside.
So he decided to enter and look for himself.
He entered, and, as he expected, the interior was indeed lavish, showing that the owner of this tower was rather rich.
He made his way up the stairway, and soon he was standing in front of the door to the room whose window he had seen open when he was outside.
"Come in."
Before he could knock, a voice came from inside, telling him to enter.
Kent opened the door, and the first thing he saw was the back of a young man sitting before the window, smoking a pipe.
He had lush silver hair that was only a bit too tall to be called short.
He was clad in royal wear, showing he was royalty.
However, around him, Kent could not see any aura that suggested he was an Immortal, God, Supreme, or even Celestial.
"You are finally here," the young man said before slowly turning to face Kent.
When their gazes met, Kent felt like he had known this person for a lifetime.
However, this feeling also came with a wave of sadness and anger, the kind that would turn the most innocent into a monster.
"You are the Ruthless Bandit," Kent asked, his eyes narrowing a bit.
The young man pulled the pipe away from his lips and let the smoke come from the corners of his mouth before a small smile appeared on his face.
"I was called that many years ago." He stood up, walked toward a chair, and sat down.
He gestured for Kent to sit down as well.
"You can call me Lex Morvane."
"I am Kent Madson."
There was just something about the way the young man was handling their meeting that kept giving Kent the creeps.
He was too polite, and on top of that, he seemed to be testing Kent in ways he didn’t even know.
"So why are you here, Kent?"
Kent narrowed his eyes, hearing this obvious question.
"Well, genius, you happen to be my incarnation, and so in my attempt to remember this life, I found myself here, so maybe cut the act and get on to helping me get what I came here for.
I am on the clock here."
Lex looked at Kent for a few seconds before a smirk appeared on his face.
"I see.
So you want to know about this life, huh?"
"Yes.
That is what I literally said."
"Oh, I see." Lex turned toward a bookshelf and picked up a book.
He brushed the dust off it and turned to Kent.
"Are you really sure you want to know about this life?

I mean, it wasn’t our best life, and while I would like you to know the horrors of the universe this early, when it comes to my life, you would learn that even the purest flower is more lethal than the most potent poison."
Kent didn’t say anything for a few seconds.
He first let Lex’s words settle in his mind for a few minutes before he nodded.
"I want to.
If I don’t know, then when would be the right time to do it?"
"If you say so.
But be aware that whatever you will be reading in this book will affect you in ways you cannot bring yourself to take for granted.
If you, in any way, feel like you can’t handle it, just close it and store it somewhere you will not be compelled to read it.
Once you recover and you feel like you can handle it one more time, then you can go for it."
Kent nodded, a bit taken aback by how Lex was handling everything.
In his mind, he would be meeting a ruthless person on a bloody battlefield, clad in tattered armor with blood covering most of his armor and even his face.
However, Lex looked like someone who had undergone therapy and had now turned a new Chapter in his life, one in which he strove to maintain the peace he sought.
This only made Kent wonder just what kind of life he had lived that had turned him into such a person.
It wasn’t normal, and that was plain as day now that he thought about it.
"Here you go," Lex handed the book over to Kent.
On the cover, he saw the book’s title, which darkened his expression.
"Birth of Evil: Tale of the Ruthless Bandit.
Vol.
The title of the book was just something he knew would contain some of the most horrifying experiences he would go through.
He already saw how Elina died during the Primordial Era and how it affected Chaos.
He also saw his life as a slave who had to endure the worst kind of torture from the day he learned to walk.
As for his life as the Faceless Assassin, he saw the lengths his mother had to go through to protect him from assassins.
But despite all those unfortunate experiences, he wouldn’t classify his life during those times as evil.
So for the Ruthless Bandit’s name to be branded as one, he knew things were about to get real.
"Remember, when it gets a bit overwhelming, just close the book and rest for a while."
Kent nodded and stored the book away.
He then looked at Lex for a few minutes before asking to leave.
"I will wait for you to come for the other volumes.
However, don’t be pressured to come, since I have nowhere else to be."
Kent nodded.
A second later, he woke up inside the tower.
He quickly reached into the tower storage and pulled out the book.
This one was much bigger than the memory diaries.
Without even opening it, Kent knew he would be reading a story instead of diary entries.
"Should I dig in right away, or should I give it a few more days to do that?
I literally have more time on my hands now that I am not moving toward the edge of the galaxy."
Kent looked at the book for a few seconds before deciding to open it and see what was inside.
Flipping to the first page, he only saw a few lines of text...
"This is the account of a beautiful life twisted by the evil of men—the tale of the one who embodied evil in all forms and essence.
Life of Lex Morvane, the Ruthless Bandit."
Kent took a deep breath, letting his mind clear.
He wanted to see what happened next, so he needed his mind settled before diving in.
A few seconds later, he turned to page two.

chapters.title: Chapter 1384: Tale Of Evil (1)
paragraphs: Man doesn’t choose to be evil; they are made into one. This is how the evil of men turns young Lex into the most ruthless being to ever walk the face of the universe.

[My name is Lex Morvana, middle child of three. I had a big sister and a little sister who I love deeply. My father is the emperor of an entire planetary system. My mom supported him in his affairs, but had more than enough time to take care of my sisters and me.
At the age of 13, I awakened my innate body, Spirit Root, and bloodline, allowing me to start cultivating much earlier and faster than many of my peers.
I was considered a prodigy by all, and because of that fame, I became everyone’s favourite.
My big sister and baby sister were my best friends. My father is the peaceful kind who can go out of his way to pardon even those who try to betray him.
By the age of 16, I had reached the Root Ascension stage, a level that made me both powerful and full of potential.
My story reached the Immortal Council, so they sent messengers to invite me to join the most prestigious sect in the Galaxy, Nine Heavens Sect.
With my family’s support, I left with them, and for 200 years, I trained hard under an Immortal Lord as my master. I went from a mortal to an Immortal within 200 years.
It was a record nobody had ever set before in the sect or anywhere. The one who came closest to my achievement took 320 years to reach the Root Immortal stage.
I was called many names and awarded many titles. However, all those names and titles meant nothing to me.
All I wanted was to see my family again. So after 200 years away, I escaped the life of a disciple and returned home.
However, what I met wasn’t what I expected.

The vibrant kingdom I left was now in ruins, ruled by people I once called family. My father’s skull was hung at the entrance of the gate. My mother, big sister, and baby sister were chained on the street, and allowed just anyone with a few gold coins to do with them as they pleased.
The maids and servants who were once my friends were either slaves working under the harshest conditions, or they were killed in the most gruesome conditions.
My heart broke into many pieces, and from that day onwards, I became a completely different person.]
Kent paused, letting the words he had read settle in. Strangely, he felt every last emotion like he was going through every moment in person.
The initial stage was sweet and perfect, putting a smile on his face. However, the latter part was now souring his mood.
He read, felt, and saw what Lex saw, and what he saw wasn’t something he loved at all.
The betrayal he was about to experience was just one that Kent was even afraid of reading. However, since he was not yet done with the page, he dove back in and continued...
[Because I was back in a High World, my cultivation was suppressed to the peak of Heavenly Ascension. This meant I couldn’t just get straight to rescuing my family.

So I did what my father told me to do whenever he wasn’t available: I went to my uncle for help. However, that was when I found out the traitor was someone I had known, respected, and even looked up to.
The man whom my father, mother, and siblings trusted the most was the one who stabbed them in the back. That discovery was the turning point for me.

So I did what I had trained to do best: I fought my way in, and after hours of struggle, I managed to rescue my family. But the darkness came when, after rescuing them, they chose death over leaving with the pain they had endured for over 50 years.

I watched them plead for me to end their suffering. I tried everything not to do it, but hearing what they went through and how long they had given up hope, I used my own two hands to take their lives.
I killed my mother and sisters not because I wanted to, but because it was the only way their suffering could end.

They had been through so much worse that breathing another breath was torture to them. So I ended their suffering, and with their death, the last bit of sympathy, empathy, love, care, and peace was washed out.
I became somebody else. I became something else. The seed of hatred took root in my heart, and with that, my clarity finally cleared.
Before my parents died, they said they had been betrayed 50 years ago by my uncle.
However, 30 years ago, I asked about how my family was doing, and my master told me they were well and that the sect is taking care of them.
20 years ago, I received a letter from my father telling me how much they missed me and that my little sister had awakened her bloodline, finally.
10 years ago, my big sister joined a powerful sect and also became an Immortal.
5 years ago, my baby sister joined her in the sect.
It was all a lie. I was lied to by my master. I was lied to by my sect. I was lied to by everyone. And for that, I will make everyone pay a million times.
I will kill them, their families, their loved ones, their children, and every single person they ever met and smiled at.
And that starts with my uncle.
My family was anything but loving and accommodating. But in the end, they suffered because of him. He destroyed all they had built and smeared their name.

So I will wipe his bloodline off the face of the universe. I do not care who is innocent in his family. As long as they have his blood in them, I, Lex Morvane, will kill every last one of them, and using their blood, I will attempt to wipe the humiliation they put my family through.]
Kent closed the book, his eyes red. Red mist could be seen coming out from the corners of his eyes and body, filling the air with the primal fury of a predator.
His anger was palpable because he had seen and felt what Lex went through. He saw how hard he came to terms with using his own hands to kill his family after suffering to rescue them.
He knew deep in his heart that killing them was the right thing to do; however, killing them wasn’t easy.
They were people he loved and cared for. They were his best friends, and so killing them was just too much for someone like him to take in.
But he did, and the outcome was his humanity turning off.
He became dead to emotions. Love, pain, and suffering were nothing to him anymore. In fact, he seemed to have become shut in, and that was when all he could feel was hatred.
Right now, his heart felt so much hatred that he just didn’t know where to put it.
"Tower, knock me out." In the end, that was the only solution he could come up with.
The tower could also sense his hatred, and so could his wives. So before the tower could even knock him out, Vexthra appeared and did it for her.
She took his body and sent him to the harem tower, laying him into a deep sleep.

chapters.title: Chapter 1385: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (1)
paragraphs: Five days after Kent was put to sleep, he woke up, feeling refreshed and less hateful.
The hatred in his heart had calmed down considerably.

Of course, even if he woke up with hatred in his heart, the fact that his head was resting on the most majestic ass in the universe and surrounded on all sides by beautiful bodies would have calmed him down considerably.
The setting he woke up in was just too perfect.
Vexthra called back her sisters, who, five days ago, were prepared to climb to the 8th floor of the dungeon. They all felt Kent’s emotions, so they all ran back.
Their man comes first in all things. His mental health is something they all value, and so when he was in trouble, they dropped everything to be with him.
Making sure he is well and happy is their job.

But now, he had recovered, and it was all thanks to every last one of them and the tower. The book with over two hundred pages left to read is back inside his tower vault, so unless he wishes to dive back in, he wouldn’t easily have access to it.
"How are you feeling?" Unity asked, cuddled up in Kent’s arm.
"I am fine, ladies." He brushed her hair and added, "I only had a backlash from recovering some of my memories. I thought I was ready, but I guess I wasn’t."
They nodded.
"You had us worried there for a second, dear," Mara said, looking a bit relieved. They were all on edge the past few days.
Mental health is a serious issue. If whatever Kent was doing was something detrimental to his mental health, then they would do everything in their power to stop him.
However, now that they have learned what had happened, they seem a bit relieved.
"Do those memories have anything to do with Elina?" Alina asked.
She is more invested in bringing Elina, whose death led to the rise of a tyrant during the primordial Era, back to the tower.
Of course, a part of why she wanted her brought to the tower is because they share the same name.
The only difference was the first letter of their names. Hers starts with ’A’ while the other starts with ’E’.𝗳𝐫𝚎𝗲𝚠𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝘃𝚎𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝗺
Aside from that, they have the same sound to their name. She has already made plans to make her a long-lost twin. So she wants to find that out.
"No, Alina, it was a new incarnation called Lex Morvane." Kent took a deep breath again. He wanted to be transparent with his wives in things he felt wouldn’t impact them negatively.
Of course, they aren’t only for sex. They are there to be his listening ears, so talking to them seems like the most logical thing he can do.

"I don’t know much about him yet, but from the little I have seen about him, it might be the most tragic life I have ever lived. He was a brilliant boy who was loved by everyone. His parents adored him, and so did his two sisters.
However, after leaving home for 200 years to advance his cultivation, he returned to find his family in ruins. His father was killed, and his head hung at the entrance of the city.
His mother and two sisters were chained and turned into fuck dolls for anyone who had a few gold coins.

He came home to meet the biggest humiliation he had ever seen being subjected on his family by someone he trusted. And when he tried to seek help, he found out that it was his uncle who had done all that.
So channeling his anger, he rescued his family, only for them to wish for death. He used his own hands to put them out of their misery, and with their death, everything good about him also died."
Kent sighed and added:
"That was all I could remember before my emotions got the best of me."
Some of his wives had tears in their eyes, while others wore frowns.

It was clear the soft-hearted ones like Unity, Val, Mara, and the others felt the impact in a more sorrowful way, while Vexthra, Neomi, Nara... felt hatred toward whoever put the family of their husband’s past incarnation through such torture.

"I am fine, ladies. It is all in the past now. I am sure I have handled it the best way I could..." A weak smile appeared on his face, already imagining what he would do if the same fate were to befall him in this life.
’I would probably burn the universe to the ground.’ His eyes narrowed a bit, and an evil intent that seemed to have come from the Ruthless Bandit seeped out from them.
"Kent, what evil thought is running through your mind?" Zaila asked, a smirk forming on her lips. She is the only one among her sisters without a sorry look or a frown.

It wasn’t that she had no emotion. She is a Mind Cultivator, so she has some form of resistance to emotions. Right now, she put those walls up so she could logically think and see if Kent was indeed alright.
"Nothing to worry about, Zaila," Kent laughed, but Zaila knew he was lying.
"If you don’t tell me, know we wouldn’t take you with us to the 8th floor."
Kent chuckled. "Seriously, it was nothing to be concerned about. I merely had a thought that would never happen, so you have nothing to worry about."

Zaila studied him long and hard, then she nodded. "I won’t pry into your thoughts. But know that I will keep a close eye on you. The first sign of abnormal behavior, and you are back in the tower, where you can have a peaceful rest."
He nodded. A few hours later, after making sure he was alright, they went to join the legions in the legion tower. Yuyin and Dia were also there.
When Dia saw Kent, she became a bit happy.

After their heart-to-heart, she felt more relieved and happy. Kent was the same. He came to the conclusion that as long as Dia was around, the pain from the curse wouldn’t be as severe as it was when he killed her in the past.
Axiom, Kailan, and Kol were also around. They managed to secure the fangs for Gaia to start building the portal, so they were now ready to go on any mission he had for them.
Kent knew they would come in handy when they started meeting Immortals in the tower. Uncle Drew also brought Enkay, his death agent, who helped locate Kaelith.
As for Kaelith, he was still unconscious in Gaiaville, the healers looking after him. It would take him some time to wake up, so they didn’t wait around for him.
"Let’s go," Vexthra said before opening the portal to the 8th floor. Since she is the leader of the legion, even with Kent around, she was allowed to lead this mission.
The portal opened, and Kaizo was the first to jump in. The others entered, and before long, every last one of them entered.
On the other side, they appeared on a ship sailing in a raging, stormy sea.
DING
The mission details appeared and everyone start to read.

But know that I will keep a close eye on you.
The first sign of abnormal behavior, and you are back in the tower, where you can have a peaceful rest."
He nodded.
A few hours later, after making sure he was alright, they went to join the legions in the legion tower.
Yuyin and Dia were also there.
When Dia saw Kent, she became a bit happy.
After their heart-to-heart, she felt more relieved and happy.
Kent was the same.
He came to the conclusion that as long as Dia was around, the pain from the curse wouldn’t be as severe as it was when he killed her in the past.
Axiom, Kailan, and Kol were also around.
They managed to secure the fangs for Gaia to start building the portal, so they were now ready to go on any mission he had for them.
Kent knew they would come in handy when they started meeting Immortals in the tower.
Uncle Drew also brought Enkay, his death agent, who helped locate Kaelith.
As for Kaelith, he was still unconscious in Gaiaville, the healers looking after him.
It would take him some time to wake up, so they didn’t wait around for him.
"Let’s go," Vexthra said before opening the portal to the 8th floor.
Since she is the leader of the legion, even with Kent around, she was allowed to lead this mission.
The portal opened, and Kaizo was the first to jump in.
The others entered, and before long, every last one of them entered.
On the other side, they appeared on a ship sailing in a raging, stormy sea.
DING
The mission details appeared and everyone start to read.

chapters.title: Chapter 1386: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (2)
paragraphs: ⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Floor Name: Greed King (8th)⟧
⟦Power Level: Empyrean⟧
⟦Description:

↠ Blue Ivy Island was once a vibrant and lush island that had been the home of the green Elves for countless years. They were ruled by the benevolent Elven King. He was a powerful Mind Cultivator whose leadership had protected his people from all kinds of threats.

↠ 15 years ago, the Elven King got greedy. He started asking for more, wanting to be more. Later, he became obsessed with breaking the limit the heavens had placed on him because he lived in a high world.
↠ His advisors did all they could to stop him before things got out of hand. However, he didn’t listen, and in the end, it became clear that his actions would put the lives of the masses in danger.
↠ So, to protect everyone, they sealed him away, bringing an end to his greed.
↠ However, 10 years ago, the seal that was used to imprison him was tampered with by an unknown person.
↠ Due to this, the Elven King started gaining his freedom, and 10 years later, the seal had reached the point where it wouldn’t hold for long.

↠ The Green Elves know they are outmatched since, from what they have sensed, their King seems to have succeeded in his endeavour. He had broken the limit and ascended to the next stage. This prompted them to call for help.

↠ However, for reasons unknown, the help they called for would never make it to the island. In three days, if help doesn’t come, they could leave the island; everything would come to an end. The green elves would be wiped from the face of the universe for good.⟧
⟦Your mission is to find a way to get to the island and kill the Greed King. Also, ensure the ships sailing to the island make it there within five days⟧
⟦Rewards⟧
↠ 40 Billion Tower Points
↠ 400 Billion Soul Essence
↠ Limit Breaker Key (Everybody)
↠ Innate Talent Awakening Pill
Kent and the team read the mission a few times before turning to look at each other. The mission was just like any other they had completed before.
However, this one seemed to have some unknown variables. The first variable concerned the person who tampered with the seal imprisoning the Elven King.
This could be someone within the ranks of the Green Elves, or perhaps someone completely outside the island. It remains unknown, but Kent would bet his money on an external threat.
So that was a big variable.
The second issue was that the aid they had requested would not reach the island in time. The storm around them was a clear sign that someone was pulling strings to prevent them from getting there.
ROAR
Suddenly, a powerful roar came from 600 meters away, just as the sea parted, and a large whale with a metallic carapace dove out of the water and slammed back in, causing the sea to surge violently.
"Hold on!"
The captain of the ship shouted, using his expertise to control the ship in order not to let the wave push them off course.
Kent used the time to turn, and what he saw made him finally understand what was happening. Behind them, over 50 ships could be seen moving in the same direction as the first ship.
It was clear this mission had just become more than killing the Greed King. The details said they should help the ships get to the island, but they said nothing about protecting 50-plus ships.
Just as he turned back to face Vexthra and the team, the captain of the ship they were on approached them.
"Excuse me, but who are you people, and where did you come from?"

Vexthra’s mind scrambled for a few seconds to come up with a logical answer that would justify why they had suddenly appeared out of nowhere and were standing on the deck of a ship that had only a few crew members and guards.
It would be rather ridiculous of her to say this was a dungeon and that they had come to clear the dungeon floor.
Or even more ridiculous to say the universe had sent them to come save them. Both answers would have made them look suspicious and a bit crazy. So she played the only card she had.
She pointed at Kent. "This is Kent Madson."
The captain turned to Kent, and for a second, he remained unmoved. Then a smile appeared on his face... "Are you really Kent Madson?"
Kent smiled and nodded. "I am."
"Awesome. I am a huge fan."

Kent glared at Vexthra before turning to the captain. "Good to meet a fan. However, I came here today not to chat—well, we can chat after this mission—but I am here to ensure you and the others make it to Blue Ivy Island."

"Okay. I am Captain Yue. It has been three days since this storm started, and it only seems to be getting worse. We tried all we could, but until the beasts causing the storm are taken care of, there is no way we can get to our destination.
But even if we could find a way around, it would take a month to get to the island."
"Rest assured, Captain Yue, we will get you to your destination. But for now, go back and keep the ship on course. Leave the rest to my team and me."
He nodded and left, feeling more relieved.
Kent turned to Vexthra. "Really, that was the best you could have done?"
She smiled. "It got the job done, didn’t it?"
"Unbelievable." Kent shook his head in amusement before asking, "So what next?"
"The mission said we have three days before it would be too late. Now that we know the ships have been stuck for three days, it is safe to say we may already be too late.
So, to get ahead of things, you will take Zaila with you and head to the island first. Kaizo will lead the rest to keep the ships on course. They will have to battle the sea beasts.
But you and Zaila must get to the island before the Greed King is freed. Since he is a Mind Cultivator, Zaila is the only one who can battle him.
Your job is to make sure no unknown variable interferes with their battle."
Kent nodded.
"We will be on our way then." Kent reached for Zaila’s hand. "Do you want to wait for me in the tower, or do you want to feel how fast I can move?"
Of course, Zaila would love that, so she jumped into his arms, causing Unity and her sisters to become jealous.
Kent smiled, and his dragon wings appeared on his back. Then, activating 50,000 flame veins, they took to the sky and vanished from sight, leaving flame trails behind them.
The ladies could only watch and wish they were in Zaila’s place. Even Vexthra and Miryssa, who are goddesses, wished for that too.
In the end, the mission was to ensure the ships reached the island.
"Alina, reinforce the ships, and Kaizo, make sure the beasts don’t come any closer to destroying any of the ships."
"Let’s go, people, time to kill some sea beasts." Kaizo turned to Ankaara. "This is your domain, so lead the way."
Ankaara, being an Ice Elemental, would be at her strongest now that she had a large mass of water at her disposal.

She moved to the edge of the ship and formed a few starry ice constructs. She threw them into the water, then closed her eyes. A few seconds later, she pointed to the west. "We have incoming. Thousands of them."
