chapters.title: Chapter 1387: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (3)
paragraphs: Kaizo led the team underwater to battle the beast and ensure that none of the ship was destroyed. Of course, to make sure everything was perfect, he left Unity, Lilian, Dia, and Yuyin on the deck to make sure no danger slipped up on them.
The rest of the legion that are above teh Heavenly Ascension stage had to stand on the side since the mission doesn’t need them.

"We are Void Beasts, so this universe has no hold on us. This means we can easily get this mission cleared within a few seconds," Axiom said, leaning lazily on the edge of the ship, watching as the water started turning red.

"We know you are awesome and all, but know that this is a training mission, so until we reach the ranks of immortals where even I or Enkay can’t handle it, that would be when you will be needed," Uncle Drew said with a slight smirk.
"How boring. It is like being back in the Void Temple all over again," Kol also exhibited his frustration, spinning an arrow between his fingers.
Vexthra shook her head and decided not to entertain them.
As a god, she could tell just how dangerous the three Void Beasts were. Kol is a Spirit Immortal, but he had the power to fight Core Immortals and even a True Immortal.

While Kailan, who is a True Immortal, could go as far as fighting Immortal Kings. As for Axiom, he is an Immortal King, but handling even an Immortal Monarch or Immortal Lord was not outside his capabilities.
So if they were that powerful, letting them handle a mission with an Empyrean as the limit was basically cheating. It would deprive the others of a good chance to train.
So for now, they would have to wait and let the youngsters have some fun.
Underwater, every last beast that tried to come any closer to the ships was being dealt with by Kaizo and his team.
Suddenly, a seahorse appeared from the east and quickly started charging a lightning blast at one of the ships, much closer to its location.

However, before it could finish charging the attack, an arrow came out of nowhere and stabbed into its head. The lightning that was being charged became unstable and exploded, taking its head off its neck.
"Awesome," Dia said, feeling happy for her sister. She could remember how impressive Artemis was with the bow, so seeing her even more impressive now filled her heart with so much joy.
Unity smiled back and started focusing more on the battle that was happening all around them, underwater.
The water started turning red as the beasts were being slaughtered.

Meanwhile, after leaving with Zaila, Kent rapidly closed in on the island. He wasn’t using his full speed or the Jade Void wings, but even with this speed, he was going so fast that within a few minutes, they had moved tens of thousands of miles.
In less than 30 minutes, the island came into sight. However, when they saw smoke coming from multiple places, Kent increased the pace.
In an instant, his speed surged, causing Zaila to tighten her hold on him, fearing she would fall.
Kent smiled and held on to her much more tightly, making her aware he had no plans on letting her fall. In a few seconds, they were hovering over the island.
It wasn’t that big, so everything that was happening was within the soul map’s coverage.
This allowed them to see the dead bodies on the ground. There were a few hundred warriors dead and a thousand locked in battle with each other.
Inside a mansion, a deep green-skinned man who looked both Elven and demonic was seated on a throne, his eyes closed, an amused expression on his face.
He seemed to be controlling the green elves to attack and kill each other.

"Looks like we are late," Kent said, looking at the battle happening on the island. His soul map showed him the thousands of Elves, some showing signs of violence, others scared beyond their understanding.
"Send me to the mansion. I will find a way to enter his mind and defeat him. You, on the other hand, must find a way to stop the battles happening all over the island."
Kent nodded. "Be careful. I will keep a close eye on you, but be careful when you face him mentally."
Zaila kissed him, and then she was sent away. The next second, she appeared inside the throne room, prompting the Green King to snap his eyes open.

An invisible mental pressure assaulted Zaila’s mind. However, she felt no discomfort whatsoever. She walked forward, and when she was close enough, her eyes changed color from the usual brown to blue.
"Let’s see whose mind will break the fastest."
Without giving the Greed King any chance, she activated mental combat. From this point forward, it would be about who had the strongest mental strength.
Zaila is a Heavenly Ascension stage mind cultivator, while the Greed King is an Empyrean. That is a single stage above her.
However, when it comes to mind cultivation, it isn’t always about the cultivation stage but more about mental strength.
Zaila sat in a lotus posture as their mental duel began in the mind realm.
On the outside, Kent remained standing in the air for a few seconds, analyzing how best to handle the battles happening all over. He could see the greed within the hearts of the elves fighting.
That was a clear sign that the Green King wasn’t only mind-controlling them; he had tapped into the greed in their hearts and weaponized it against them.
That was why, even when Zaila challenged him to a mental duel, the battle didn’t stop. His hold on them wasn’t just to kill them but to amplify the greed in their hearts and take it for himself.
It took Kent a moment to figure that one out. But even when he did, he found no way to cut that connection.
’Tower, if I manage to knock them out, would that solve the problem?’

[No, master. Even when they are unconscious, the Green King can still siphon the greed in their hearts. The only way is to kill them or find the connection between them and the Greed King and cut it.]
’Oh, that is going to be a bit difficult,’ Kent smiled. ’If I were to be an ordinary person, that is.’

He blinked a few times, then he activated the Heavenly Jade Eye. At once, he could see thousands of strings coming from the mansion where the Greed King was, each linking to the soul of every last elf on the island.
"How insidious," Kent said, a bit disturbed at seeing strings linked to even babies.
He quickly came up with a way to handle that. He opened the soul universe and started flooding the entire island with soul essence.

The only way to stop this was to cut the strings. However, learning that even babies had been affected, he decided to first protect their souls. This way, when he started cutting the strings, no harm would come to them.
The mission this time indeed had variables, and one of them was seeing babies affected by the attack of someone who was once their king.
The second variable was, of course, the shadows slowly moving toward his direction from the moment he and Zaila arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 1388: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (4)
paragraphs: [Zaila’s POV]
Just like how there are sword realms for swordsmen, mind cultivators also have a mental realm where, on a certain level, they can challenge each other to see who has the strongest mind.
Depending on how strong the mind is, the stronger the mental realm would also become.
Zaila went straight for a mental duel because of the advantage she had when it came to using the mental realm.
She had already awakened her mind space, and so she could easily make good use of it.
So the moment she issued the challenge, their consciousness was sent to the mind space, where both their mental realms had activated.
Behind the Greed King, a large dark skull with hollow eye sockets, burning furiously, hovered, staring dangerously at Zaila. It was clear that her interruption had made the Greed King very angry.
However, as he stared at what hovered behind Zaila, he seemed a bit apprehensive.

"I have been waiting for this moment for a very long time," Zaila said, a smile appearing on her face. "I never had the chance to see how strong my mind had become after reaching the Heavenly Ascension stage, so you can only imagine my happiness when I found you are a mind cultivator."
The Greed King tried to speak, but Zaila raised her finger to stop him.
"I will allow you to attack me with all you have. If you manage to kill me, fine, but when I get bored, then know your ending will come swiftly, and in the most agonizing way you can imagine.
And well, you are in my mind prison now, so unless I want you to leave, you cannot even move an inch."
Behind Zaila, a large disc featuring hundreds of segmentations hovered, slowly spinning.
To the ordinary folk, it was merely a disc, but to someone like the Greed King, who is a mind cultivator, he knew every mind cultivator’s dream was to awaken what now hovered behind Zaila.
It is called the Mind Disc. It connects to one innate mind system, allowing them to create some of the most powerful mind attacks they can devise.
The best part is that whatever they create and put into a mind segment can later be refined and improved.
The Greed King sensed the danger because, from what he knew, filling just one mind segment is enough to make the owner a terrifying foe.

Zaila had filled three segments. This means she had created three dangerous abilities that she could use at will. So despite him being a realm higher than Zaila, he seemed to sense the danger, and as such, he hesitated to attack.
"Oh, if you are stalling for time, then know my partner will soon cut the connection between you and the elves."

Hearing what Zaila said, the expression on the Greed King’s face changed. He formed a hand seal, and at once, one of the green sockets on the skull lit up. A beam formed and, without delay, it fired forward with deadly speed.
The attack came with a deadly intent, something that would scare anyone.

However, Zaila merely snapped her finger, and one of the mind segments on the mind disc glowed. A rune flew from it, and just before the beam could land on her body, a dark portal opened and swallowed the beam.
The Greed King’s expression turned dark in an instant.
"Guess where that went."
Zaila pointed up, prompting the Greed King to look up as well. There, to his horror, another dark portal opened, and the beam fired at Zaila came out, aimed at his head.
He took a step back and threw his hand forward, causing the skull to move and hover between him and the beam.

The beam slammed into the skull with a deafening mental clang, ripples spreading through the mental realm like cracks across glass. The skull trembled violently, its hollow eye sockets flaring as fragments of dark energy scattered into the void-like space around them.
The Greed King narrowed his eyes, finally discarding any trace of amusement.
"So that is your trick," he said coldly. "Spatial inversion within a mind realm. Interesting."
Zaila smiled faintly and pointed up again. "It is much more than that, buddy."
Just when she said that, the portal opened, and the same beam that had just landed on the skull appeared, this time with more deadly speed and intent.
"W-What..." The Greed King narrowed his eyes, the look of shock and fear appearing in them. He formed another hand seal and channelled more mental energy into the skull before the beam landed on it.
He defended against the attack, but the backlash pushed him back a few steps.
"My trick goes way beyond spatial inversion, buddy. When I was a Core Formation mind cultivator, I only had spatial inversion, but later I changed it into something else.
Now, instead of just inverting your attack, I can use it repeatedly and make it even more deadly, provided I have the energy to sustain it.
So, how about you help me see to what extent I can take this new trick of mine?"

Zaila pointed up again, and the portal formed. This time, the green beam that appeared was much darker and super fast. When it landed on the skull, a powerful shockwave followed, pushing the Greed King back.
As for the skull, a dent appeared in it.
"Again," Zaila yet again pointed up, and an even more deadly beam appeared. When it landed on the skull, cracks began to appear.
"I know I wanted you to attack me till I get bored, but since we are here now, you might as well enjoy it."
The Greed King spat a mouthful of blood as he formed more seals with his left hand.

On the outside, blood started seeping from the corner of his mouth. The initial amused smile on his face was nowhere to be seen. This time, he had a frown on, a clear sign that he was having a really bad day.
As for Zaila, she stood with her beautiful expression still the same. An amused smirk could even be seen tugging at the corner of her lips.
Clearly, Kent underestimated just how dangerous she was. He was worried for nothing. In fact, if she were to meet even a Life or Death stage mind cultivator, she would be fine.
Inside the mental space, the skull let out a silent scream as dark mist poured from its jaws, flooding the mental realm.
The mist twisted into clawed shapes, each one radiating corrosive greed, lunging toward Zaila from all directions.
She didn’t move.
The moment the mist crossed a certain distance, invisible walls formed around her. The clawed shapes slammed into them and shattered, dissolving into fragments of unstable intent.
"H-How is this even possible?"
He took several steps back, his expression turning even darker now. With nothing but a mental command, his perfectly crafted attack was dismantled.
Zaila smirked. "No need to be in shock, buddy. I have thousands of years of experience, so someone like you is merely an ant before my eyes."
As if to prove it to him, Zaila pointed up, then she snapped her finger.

At once, over twenty portals opened, and from within, terrifying beams blasted out, each aimed at the poor king, who managed to use the greed in his heart to break the limit placed on him by the universe, only to meet a monster like her.
On the outside, Kent had flooded the entire island with soul essence, making sure every last Green Elf was affected by the soul universe.
However, just when he was getting ready for the second phase of his plan, five shadows rose from the ground and transformed into five beings.

chapters.title: Chapter 1389: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (5)
paragraphs: Kent had already sensed the shadows long before they appeared.
However, when they showed up and transformed into Dark Fiends, he became a bit stunned. Among the many beings he wanted to meet on this mission, Dark Fiends were the last on his list.
Vexthra had already told him about their encounter on the 5th floor, when they battled the Dark Princess and her dark fiends.
That revealed that she had already begun her invasion and had many seeds scattered across the universe, waiting to hatch.𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶
Provided the conditions are met, she would be able to unleash her complete strength in no time.
However, while learning all that seemed a bit alarming, meeting dark fiends twice already in the dungeon-clearing mission seemed a bit coincidental.
There was just no way this was random. There had to be some form of meaning to all that; there always is a hidden meaning when things like this happen.
"So you five were the outliers, huh?" Kent said, turning to face them. All five of them had taken on the look of 3-meter-tall goat men.
They had the head of a goat and the body of a man. Of course, they stood on their hind legs, showing they had hooves instead of toes.
"Who are you, and why are you interfering in the business of the Elves?" one of the Dark Fiends asked in a furious tone.

Kent grinned, then he answered, "They are family. You see, my mom’s uncle’s brother’s sister’s grandma’s grandfather’s aunt’s nephew’s great-grandpa’s friend’s best friend was once a green elf, so when I sensed they were in danger, I came to offer my help."
He narrowed his eyes at the five dark fiends and asked, "Do you have any problem with that, Dark Fiends?"
Although they had the head of a goat, a look of shock appeared on their faces. Being recognized by Kent was the last thing they wanted or expected.
This mission was one they were sent on by the Dark Princess, or at least a part of her. She wanted something from the green elves, but to get it, she needed the Greed King.
So she sent her dark fiends to come get it for her. However, she warned them that, unless necessary, they could never show their true selves.
They followed that instruction to the T; however, Kent could tell their true nature with a mere glance. That was just something they never expected.
"No need to deny it. I can tell a Dark Fiend from a mile away, so instead of denying it, how about you tell me what you want, and maybe we can come to an agreement."
"Or you can die." All five dark fiends charged forward, their bodies engulfed in dark, misty flame. They wanted him dead in an instant, so they went all out from the start.
However, after taking a few steps, they all came to a halt, and then they dropped to their knees, all five of them.

Kent tapped into his Blood Runes, using the pressure to suppress them. He rendered them immobile in an instant using just the power of his aura"Relax for now, lads, I have to free these folks form a puppet master first. You know, because they are family."
Kent turned away from them, leaving them suppressed under the bone-crushing weight of his aura. Recalling Chaos, Jest, and Faceless memories to that extent seemed to have transformed his aura.

So, adding just ten thousand blood runes, he was able to suppress five Empyreans. And what was even more shocking was that these five dark fiends seemed to have some form of bloodline power, something dark fiends, from what he knew, shouldn’t have.
This showed he had become very powerful but also, the dark fiends are now different from how they were before.
After he turned away, he extended his hand, and Gaap appeared in his firm grip. Then his Heavenly Jade Eye changed from gold to dark-gold, with a hint of red in there somewhere.
With the change, his level 9 heavenly sword aura exploded from his sword, filling the entire island.
Just like with his aura, his sword aura had also undergone so many changes. This was mainly because of Jest. In his memories, he had become a Sword Legend with a level 9 Divine sword aura.
Thanks to that knowledge, his understanding of sword aura had reached a whole new level.
He raised his sword, and under the stunned yet furious looks of the five dark fiends, he took a simple swing.
All over the island, the battle happening came to a halt. The strings binding them to the Greed King were all severed.
It was so effortless that nobody felt any pain when he cut the strings.
He stored away the sword, then, using his energy, he amplified his voice.

"My name is Kent Madson. I was sent here by the Goddess of Light to save you. So all able men and women should help those injured and the children to the shore. Ships are coming to take you to safety."

After saying that, Kent turned to the five dark fiends and grinned. "Here is how we are going to do this. I have some questions for you five. As to how detailed and precise your answers are, I will choose to let you go or kill you."
He raised his hand and gestured down again, causing even more pressure to be pressed down on them. "I hope I am understood."
Even if he wasn’t understood, considering the pressure on them, they nodded.
"Good." Kent snapped his finger, and the pressure vanished. However, tapping into his sword intent, he surrounded all five of them with invisible swords.
They felt them, and well, they felt the sharpness in the air, so they became still, not daring to even move their heads.
Seeing this, Kent smiled...
Inside the Mind Space, Zaila stood calmly in the air, her expression amused. On the other hand, the Greed King seemed to have offended the executioner.
His body was littered with cuts, blood oozing from his mouth and nose. Even his body was releasing more blood than the amount coming from his mouth and nose.
For a while, he was holding on quite well.
However, the moment Kent cut the connection between him and the green elves, his source of power was taken from him, causing him to rapidly run out of energy.
The skull had long shattered, with the only thing remaining being the fractured half of its jaw.
"One bad thing about borrowing energy from a third party is that the moment they are taken away from you, everything comes crashing down."
Zaila took a step forward, and soon she was standing over the Greed King’s weakened body.
"You could have walked the natural path and ascended like a normal human. But your greed to rule above all made you complacent, and that is why you will be dying now."

She pointed her finger at him. "Learn to walk the natural line drawn by the heavens in your next life." A thin needle formed at the tip of her finger and went through his head, ending him in the mind space.
On the outside, his eyes widened, then they dimmed. He fell forward from his throne and landed on the ground.
Zaila looked at all this happening and merely let a smile appear on her face. She spread out her senses to see where Kent was.
What she saw left her stunned and a bit amused.

chapters.title: Chapter 1390: The Eighth Floor - Greed King (6)
paragraphs: All over the island, the Elves, following Kent’s command, started moving to the Eastern shore, where the ships are on their way to come pick them.
Because they had been living in isolation for a long time, they had only heard rumours of Kent.
Those among them who sometimes went to get supplies heard that the entire universe was looking for someone called Kent Madson.
They weren’t like the other races out there who had heard and witnessed immortals descend to their planets to look for him.
So in a way, they had no reason to heed his command.

However, when he gave them the command, every last one of them obeyed. Even if they didn’t want to, the fact that they were under attack by a threat they couldn’t defeat made Kent stepping in the best thing that ever happened to them.
So they quickly sent the injured and the children there while the warriors among them worked to protect them. The battle had ended, but they were still on their guard.
The fact that they had attacked each other without showing any restraint made them see how weak they were and how close they had come to personal annihilation.
However, while they worked to gather their people, Kent stood in the air, his expression calm as he gazed at the five dark fiends.
They stood still, their expressions dark.
Suddenly, Zaila appeared beside him, her gaze narrowed at the five dark fiends. Just like Kent, she also recognised them as dark fiends.
"Don’t tell me there is another Dark Princess here," Zaila said, her gaze narrowing faintly.
Kent smiled and said, "That is why you are here. Get inside their minds and tell me what they know."
Zaila nodded.

Kent knew that if he asked the five dark fiends to snitch on their master, there was a chance they would die. Most powerful beings like the Dark Queen would never allow their subordinates to reveal any secrets.
They would place a curse on them to ensure that whenever they were forced to say anything that would infringe on their safety, they would die.
However, while their sudden deaths would actually allow Kent to steal their memories, whenever the curse was triggered, their minds would be wiped clean before they even died.
So he needed someone like Zaila to get into their minds to get what he wanted.
"Remember, since the Dark Queen created them, there is a chance she might have a defence mechanism in place to prevent you from entering. So be careful."
Zaila nodded and closed her eyes. When she opened them, they turned blue, like how they were when she took the Greed King to the Mind Space.
Yet again, she invoked that mind attack. However, instead of taking them to the Mind Space, she entered their minds through their eyes.
One second, she was staring at five dark fiends; the next, she appeared before a towering statue, one that looked both imposing and extremely terrifying.
It was a statue of a lady with three heads, twelve eyes, and six arms. She had two pairs of eyes on each head, amounting to twelve across all three heads.
The moment Zaila saw this statue, she summoned her Mind Disc.
"There would be no need, mortal. You cannot get what you came here for." Before Zaila could make her move, an ancient voice came from the head facing her.
Then a terrifying pressure fell from the sky and slammed hard on her. This forced her to her knees, and on the outside, blood seeped from the corner of her lips.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
"HMMMM," Kent hummed, then he walked toward one of the dark fiends and pressed his finger against its forehead.
His eyes turned red, and at once, a profound aura burst out of him.
"BE GONE." A voice that shook the heavens and the earth slammed into the statue, cracking it.
"What?" the ancient voice shouted, but before she could attempt to repair the damage, the second mind segment on the Mind Disc glowed, and the rune transformed into a giant sword.
It extended about 400 meters and was 150 meters wide. Its sheer size dwarfed the statue by several meters.
"You heard my husband. Be gone." The sword moved and landed on the chest of the statue. The impact was so violent that it rattled the statue first before shattering it completely.

The statue crumbled, and in its place, vast runes of memories revealed themselves, allowing Zaila to start taking them. The space started to crack, so she merely stole them, which she would later translate.
On the outside, cracks started appearing on the bodies of the five dark fiends. A few seconds later, they shattered. Zaila was quick to escape before they died.
If she had been a second late, perhaps she would be unconscious now.
"That was dangerous," Zaila said, taking a deep breath.
Kent hugged her from behind. "I know. Sorry for putting you in danger."

"It is nothing. You protected me in the end, so there is nothing to be guilty about..." She turned and looked at him, then asked, "Though, I have to ask, how did you do that? I mean, that was a god consciousness in the statue, right? So how did you manage to stun her and even cause the statue to crack?"
Kent smiled and scratched his head. "It was a Supreme, and well, I merely used the power of my bloodline. You can do the same if I give you permission."
Zaila looked at Kent for a few minutes before she muttered, "You are a freak of nature." She planted her face on his chest and exhaled deeply.
Learning she had just shattered a statue that held the consciousness of a supreme being made her a bit proud.
However, hearing how Kent managed to free her from the mental suppression and even buy her ample time to shatter the statue finally told her just what kind of monster her man was.
"No need to be stunned, dear. I am just awesome."
Kent carried her in a princess carry and vanished into the tower. They appeared in the Harem Tower and quickly took her to her treehouse and laid her down to sleep.
She had exhausted her mind, so she needed to rest for a few hours at least before diving back into translating the memories she had stolen.
She slipped into a deep sleep the next second.
Kent covered her body with a warm cloth before returning to the island.

He learned from Chaos’s memories that the name of his bloodline held some power. Of course, before then, he had learned from Flame Lord Agni that his name could be harnessed by others as long as he gave them his permission.
However, he had long forgotten about that until recently, when he recovered Chaos’s memories.
So when Zaila faced an obstacle she couldn’t handle, he tapped into his bloodline and, using his connection with her, invoked his bloodline power in just two words.

That did the trick, bringing an end to the 8th-floor mission and opening the door for a much bigger mission that he would probably go on while Gaia worked on the portal that would take him to the edge of the galaxy.
Three days later, the ships arrived at the shore of the island.

sentences.text: All over the island, the Elves, following Kent’s command, started moving to the Eastern shore, where the ships are on their way to come pick them.
Because they had been living in isolation for a long time, they had only heard rumours of Kent.
Those among them who sometimes went to get supplies heard that the entire universe was looking for someone called Kent Madson.
They weren’t like the other races out there who had heard and witnessed immortals descend to their planets to look for him.
So in a way, they had no reason to heed his command.
However, when he gave them the command, every last one of them obeyed.
Even if they didn’t want to, the fact that they were under attack by a threat they couldn’t defeat made Kent stepping in the best thing that ever happened to them.
So they quickly sent the injured and the children there while the warriors among them worked to protect them.
The battle had ended, but they were still on their guard.
The fact that they had attacked each other without showing any restraint made them see how weak they were and how close they had come to personal annihilation.
However, while they worked to gather their people, Kent stood in the air, his expression calm as he gazed at the five dark fiends.
They stood still, their expressions dark.
Suddenly, Zaila appeared beside him, her gaze narrowed at the five dark fiends.
Just like Kent, she also recognised them as dark fiends.
"Don’t tell me there is another Dark Princess here," Zaila said, her gaze narrowing faintly.
Kent smiled and said, "That is why you are here.
Get inside their minds and tell me what they know."
Zaila nodded.
Kent knew that if he asked the five dark fiends to snitch on their master, there was a chance they would die.
Most powerful beings like the Dark Queen would never allow their subordinates to reveal any secrets.
They would place a curse on them to ensure that whenever they were forced to say anything that would infringe on their safety, they would die.
However, while their sudden deaths would actually allow Kent to steal their memories, whenever the curse was triggered, their minds would be wiped clean before they even died.
So he needed someone like Zaila to get into their minds to get what he wanted.
"Remember, since the Dark Queen created them, there is a chance she might have a defence mechanism in place to prevent you from entering.
So be careful."
Zaila nodded and closed her eyes.
When she opened them, they turned blue, like how they were when she took the Greed King to the Mind Space.
Yet again, she invoked that mind attack.
However, instead of taking them to the Mind Space, she entered their minds through their eyes.
One second, she was staring at five dark fiends; the next, she appeared before a towering statue, one that looked both imposing and extremely terrifying.
It was a statue of a lady with three heads, twelve eyes, and six arms.
She had two pairs of eyes on each head, amounting to twelve across all three heads.
The moment Zaila saw this statue, she summoned her Mind Disc.
"There would be no need, mortal.
You cannot get what you came here for." Before Zaila could make her move, an ancient voice came from the head facing her.
Then a terrifying pressure fell from the sky and slammed hard on her.
This forced her to her knees, and on the outside, blood seeped from the corner of her lips.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
"HMMMM," Kent hummed, then he walked toward one of the dark fiends and pressed his finger against its forehead.
His eyes turned red, and at once, a profound aura burst out of him.
"BE GONE." A voice that shook the heavens and the earth slammed into the statue, cracking it.
"What?" the ancient voice shouted, but before she could attempt to repair the damage, the second mind segment on the Mind Disc glowed, and the rune transformed into a giant sword.
It extended about 400 meters and was 150 meters wide.
Its sheer size dwarfed the statue by several meters.
"You heard my husband.
Be gone." The sword moved and landed on the chest of the statue.
The impact was so violent that it rattled the statue first before shattering it completely.
No...
N-No...
N-N-No..."
The statue crumbled, and in its place, vast runes of memories revealed themselves, allowing Zaila to start taking them.
The space started to crack, so she merely stole them, which she would later translate.
On the outside, cracks started appearing on the bodies of the five dark fiends.
A few seconds later, they shattered.
Zaila was quick to escape before they died.
If she had been a second late, perhaps she would be unconscious now.
"That was dangerous," Zaila said, taking a deep breath.
Kent hugged her from behind.
"I know.
Sorry for putting you in danger."
"It is nothing.
You protected me in the end, so there is nothing to be guilty about..." She turned and looked at him, then asked, "Though, I have to ask, how did you do that?
I mean, that was a god consciousness in the statue, right?
So how did you manage to stun her and even cause the statue to crack?"
Kent smiled and scratched his head.
"It was a Supreme, and well, I merely used the power of my bloodline.
You can do the same if I give you permission."
Zaila looked at Kent for a few minutes before she muttered, "You are a freak of nature." She planted her face on his chest and exhaled deeply.
Learning she had just shattered a statue that held the consciousness of a supreme being made her a bit proud.
However, hearing how Kent managed to free her from the mental suppression and even buy her ample time to shatter the statue finally told her just what kind of monster her man was.
"No need to be stunned, dear.
I am just awesome."
Kent carried her in a princess carry and vanished into the tower.
They appeared in the Harem Tower and quickly took her to her treehouse and laid her down to sleep.

chapters.title: Chapter 1391: Destiny Child
paragraphs: "So that was what happened," Kent finished his narrative on what happened when he and Zaila came to the rescue of the green Elves.

"Unbelievable. I can’t believe a second Dark Princess, or perhaps even a Dark Queen, had appeared yet again in the dungeon," Vexthra turned and looked at what remained of the bodies of the Dark Fiends.
Just as Kent expected, they all became a bit stunned to learn that the hidden source of the danger they faced on the just-ended mission was the dark fiends.
It was not a coincidence, yet it was a coincidence, depending on how one saw it.
It wasn’t a coincidence, since they learned the Dark Queen had spread her seeds across the universe. She had already told them that when they killed a copy of her on the fifth floor.
So seeing yet another sign of her presence on the 8th floor wasn’t much of a coincidence.
But it was a coincidence in the sense that when they first met her, they didn’t learn much from her, not as much as what Kent and Zaila may have just done.

Right now, they have a deep secret about the Dark Queen that they could easily use against her. It wasn’t much, but considering she went out of her way to shield the minds of her dark fiends said quite a lot.
So it was a coincidence that the dungeon had spawned yet another Dark Princess for them, mainly to gain something from her.
"The reason Zaila is now tired and asleep is that she managed to extract the memories of the Dark Fiends before they died. Once she wakes up, we will know more."
Everyone nodded.
Kent turned toward the ships loading the green elves. "Do we know where they are taking them?" he asked.

"Yes. Captain Yue said they are taking them to the Elven Forest. It is a sacred continent for all kinds of elves. After the mission ended, I scanned the planet and found it to be a good place for them to stay.
There is no need to take them into the tower, since they have somewhere both peaceful and welcoming."
"That is good to hear. As long as they have somewhere to go, then all we can do is make sure they get there in one piece."
Vexthra nodded.
The tower was for those who had nowhere else to go. They could find a new home with them. However, as long as they had a home, they could only make sure they got there safely and in one piece.

"Don’t worry, Veera will leave one of her undead with them. If something bad were to happen, we would know immediately and come to their aid. But for now, let them experience the natural flow of their lives."

By the end of the day, the ships were loaded and departed. Kaizo yet again led the team to protect them, while Kent and some of his wives remained on the island to look for the clues left behind by the dungeon.

Also, the dark fiends came because the green elves had something that only the Greed King could give them. Kent wanted to know what, and since Zaila was not yet back, looking the old-fashioned way was the only option for them.
Meanwhile, far away in an Immortal world, a lady stood from what appeared to be a throne, her expression pale.
Looking at her aura, she was a True Immortal with four Immortal Qi. However, she didn’t look like a big shot right now. If anything, she looked more like someone who had seen a ghost.
She is the Dark Queen or, at least, a copy of herself that she aimed to use to amass strength and power before her true awakening.

Years ago, she discovered a secret of Blue Ivy Island. This secret was something that, if she got her hands on it, she could easily advance to the Immortal King or even the Immortal Emperor stage without much stress and danger.
So she sent her Dark Fiends to get it for her. Initially, they tried but found that the only way to get it was for the Greed King to willingly hand it over.
So they tampered with the seal that held him prisoner and signed a contract with him.
The contract simply meant they would help him become an Immortal, which started with him killing every last green elf, and he would give them the Heart of the Island.
They came this close, but everything came crashing down when Kent and his people arrived.
However, what shook her wasn’t the fact that her dark fiends had died and the mission failed; it was what happened when Zaila tried stealing the memories of the dark fiends.
"That isn’t possible, right?"
She muttered, the paleness on her face turning even whiter.

"Invocation can only be done by the Destiny Child. The last Destiny Child fell during the Primordial Era, as far as I know. So how was he able to invoke such a terrifying power to the point of even wounding my mind?"
The disbelief on her face only turned paler.

It seemed she knew what Kent did, and, based on what she knew, that shouldn’t have been possible. But even if it wasn’t possible, the fact that Kent had wounded her told her that, no matter what, the brat could not be allowed to live for long.
He is a danger to her and everyone around her.
Invoking bloodline power was something only the True Primordials could do. Kent was a True Primordial, and so he could use it. He could also allow others to do the same.
So if such a person was allowed to live for long, there was no telling what he would become.
"Somebody," she called out, and a dark fiend with lady-like features appeared in the room and knelt down.
"Spread the word. A Destiny Child is born, and his name is Kent Madson."

"As you command, my queen." The lady left, and soon, the words of the rebirth of a Destiny Child began spreading through the criminal underworld. The criminal underworld would hate to have a Destiny Child running around.
While Kent can’t use his invocation powers frequently, whenever he used them, the damage he could cause would be so devastating that none of them wanted him alive for long.
As word continued to spread, it soon started reaching the ears of the so-called righteous faction.
They claimed they walked the path of the heavens and that their sacred duty was to protect the Universe from all forms of harm.
The Celestial Council ruled over them with the Supreme Celestial Being, the Overlord of all. He is the son of the universe, according to his claim.
When he received word that a Destiny Child had been born and that his name matched the person he had been looking for, his expression changed a bit.
To someone like him, who had lived a very long life, he knew more secrets of the universe than anyone. So he knew a Destiny Child was a child of the Universe.
This meant the rightful heir of the universe was not him, but Kent, and as such, he could not allow him to rise and ascend where he couldn’t.

chapters.title: Chapter 1392: Soul Temple
paragraphs: [Five Days Later]
Five days later, Kent and his wives had searched everywhere on the island but found nothing from the dungeon or what the dark fiends were after.
On the previous floors, they usually find something that either links to Unity’s past or a treasure for all of them to enjoy.
"Looks like there is nothing more for Unity to remember, so the dungeon stopped leaving stuff for us to find," Selene said, taking a seat on a stone with a whitish surface.
A few of her sisters joined her.
"It seems so. But that doesn’t explain why we also couldn’t find what the dark fiends were after."
They had already examined the body of the Greed King and found nothing on him that suggested he had something for the dark fiends.
So it is either that they are missing something, or they really had nothing left to find.
"Everything will make sense when Zaila is up."
It had already been five days on the outside since the battle came to an end, so by now, Zaila had woken up or was nearing the time to wake up.
Since she has the memories from the dark fiends, she would know something that they could use before heading to the 9th floor.
"Kaizo said they had reached the other side of the sea and are now leading the elves to their new home. So, since we have nothing left here to find, I suggest we go back to the tower."
They all accepted Kent’s suggestion and quickly returned to the harem tower. When they arrived, Zaila was already up, but she had been meditating for a while now.
They allowed her to remain in her meditative state for a few hours.
"Sorry for the delay. After the battle, I gained some insight into my cultivation, and so I spent the time making the best of it."
Facing someone whose consciousness had already reached the rank of a supreme made her go all out. But by doing so, she identified the gaps in her Mind Disc. This helped her fix them.
After a couple of weeks of meditation, she had addressed those limitations.
The next time she met someone like the Dark Queen, she would be ready.
"I have also translated the memories, and while we managed to prevent them from getting what they came for, there is a much bigger problem left to handle."
"What did they come for?" Vexthra asked.
"There is something on the island called the Island Heart. It is like the core of a beast, only that this core can only be accessed by the Elven King.
By killing him, we prevented them from having it. However, now that he is dead, we cannot have it either. Honestly, I think that is for the best, since none of us is ready to kill a living island."
The ladies and Kent raised their brows, hearing what Zaila said.
None of them expected to hear that the island they had just returned from was a living entity and that the dark fiends came for its soul. That was the last thing they expected.
For an island to have a heart means it has undergone some form of evolution that makes it worthy of being called a living thing.
Such a thing cannot be killed easily. If left to grow and improve, it can one day awaken an innate body and innate sentience, and even become a living person.
When Faceless was left in the Evergreen Forest by his mother, he met many sentient plants—some benevolent, others extremely evil. The good ones helped him many times.
Later, when he became a big shot, he helped many of them awaken their innate bodies and become living beings.
Some of the great healers that once walked the face of the universe, and others still living now, are either Plantkin or descendants of a long-forgotten race affiliated with the Plantkin.
He is aware of the kind of life things like this island can have if they are allowed to grow. And for an island that had protected the green elves for years, he knew it must be one of the good ones.
’Tower, tell me, can we move this island into the tower?’

Since he is in favour of not killing the island, then helping it grow is the next best thing. The Dark Queen failed once to secure the island heart. However, there is no telling whether she won’t find another way to win next time.

[The master can indeed move the island, but you will require the expertise of Akira. She is a Soul Weaver, so if she can weave an array into the core of the island, then technically, we can move it into the tower for good.]
’Good to know that,’ Kent said inwardly.
He wants to protect the island because, if what he had experienced in the past were to come to pass again, he would have a powerful being by his side to face what he would have to face in the future.
"How about the memories?"
"That one was basically about the island heart and where they came from. It turns out they are from the Immortal Realm and were created by a Dark Queen rather than a dark princess.
This already makes her a threat. However, as for how they managed to find this island, there is a small memory obtained illegally by one of the Dark Fiends.
He overheard the Dark Queen speaking to someone and referred to the person as an envoy of the Soul Temple."
Everyone except Vexthra became lost in what Zaila had just said. There is just no way they understood or knew who this Soul Temple is.
But Vexthra does.
"The Soul Temple is the biggest threat in the universe. They are the opposite of the Righteous Faction." She paused and let her mind settle before she continued to speak.

"From what I know, after the Great War, two factions rose. The Righteous Faction, led by the Celestial Council and ruled by the Supreme Celestial. They became protectors of the universe, or so they claim.
They are not perfect, but from the history books, they have come through for the universe in every era.
Then there is the Soul Temple. They claim the universe needs correction, and so, for years, they have done everything they could to bring the universe to its knees.
They have aided the Calamity Beasts, Shadow Creatures, Dark Creatures, and every other threat that came for the universe in the past.

Their power and influence are so great that not even the Celestial Council was able to destroy them. In fact, from what I know, they are far more deadly than the Righteous Faction could afford to mess with.
So they let them be, and for years, their circle only grew. They have eyes and ears everywhere, and if they want something done, they have a million and one ways to get it done.

If they are the ones aiding the Dark Queen, then there is a 100% guarantee she would be reborn, and since her consciousness is that of a supreme, we can already see she would be coming back as a supreme."
The ladies looked stunned, unsure of how to process what Vexthra had just said.
Even Kent was a bit stunned. He had yet to learn anything about the Soul Temple from all three of his lives after the Chaos Dragon fell during the Primordial Era.
Of course, he wasn’t much of a threat in his life as Lord Genesis, but he had his fair share of encounters as the Faceless Assassin.
But even so, he had yet to meet these people. This is a clear sign that they are not a simple organization.
"One last thing, their greatest achievement was killing the Night Riders,"
"WHAT,"

Everyone except Vexthra became lost in what Zaila had just said.
There is just no way they understood or knew who this Soul Temple is.
But Vexthra does.
"The Soul Temple is the biggest threat in the universe.
They are the opposite of the Righteous Faction." She paused and let her mind settle before she continued to speak.
"From what I know, after the Great War, two factions rose.
The Righteous Faction, led by the Celestial Council and ruled by the Supreme Celestial.
They became protectors of the universe, or so they claim.
They are not perfect, but from the history books, they have come through for the universe in every era.
Then there is the Soul Temple.
They claim the universe needs correction, and so, for years, they have done everything they could to bring the universe to its knees.
They have aided the Calamity Beasts, Shadow Creatures, Dark Creatures, and every other threat that came for the universe in the past.
Their power and influence are so great that not even the Celestial Council was able to destroy them.
In fact, from what I know, they are far more deadly than the Righteous Faction could afford to mess with.
So they let them be, and for years, their circle only grew.
They have eyes and ears everywhere, and if they want something done, they have a million and one ways to get it done.

If they are the ones aiding the Dark Queen, then there is a 100% guarantee she would be reborn, and since her consciousness is that of a supreme, we can already see she would be coming back as a supreme."
The ladies looked stunned, unsure of how to process what Vexthra had just said.
Even Kent was a bit stunned.
He had yet to learn anything about the Soul Temple from all three of his lives after the Chaos Dragon fell during the Primordial Era.
Of course, he wasn’t much of a threat in his life as Lord Genesis, but he had his fair share of encounters as the Faceless Assassin.
But even so, he had yet to meet these people.
This is a clear sign that they are not a simple organization.
"One last thing, their greatest achievement was killing the Night Riders,"
"WHAT,"

chapters.title: Chapter 1393: How The Night Riders Fell
paragraphs: Hearing that the Night Riders were killed by the Soul Temple finally made Kent realise the kind of danger they were in.
The soul temple is a threat, and he can tell that now. This means he must be wary of them for now.
He quickly led everyone to the legion tower to hear from Uncle Drew’s own mouth, since he is the one Night Rider whose memories had returned in full.
"Master, are we leaving already?" Vargus asked, already prepared to watch the youngsters in the legion battle on the 9th floor. He is a demigod, so he had no business fighting now.
But he enjoys watching them fight. It helps him analyse their fighting style and better support them during training sessions.

"No, buddy, I need to have a conversation with Uncle Drew." Kaizo isn’t the only one who seems to like battle. Vargus is the same, and he most certainly will have his turn as they climb higher in the dungeon.
"Go ahead, young master, what do you wanna know?"
"We can start by telling me how you died during the Dark Era."
Uncle Drew raised his brow, turning to look at the ladies standing beside Kent. Seeing they knew something, he nodded and started to reveal how the infamous Night Riders met their end.
"Four hundred thousand years before the Dark War, we received a mission from the Celestial Council to kill a powerful cultivator known by all as the Ruthless Bandit."

The ladies turned and looked at Kent. When he woke up a couple of weeks ago, he talked about the life he had just started recalling. However, he failed to mention that it was the life of the Ruthless Bandit.
But, a couple of hours ago, Unity asked, and he had no choice but to tell them he was the Ruthless Bandit, one of the most evil people ever to walk the face of the universe.
Now, however, they couldn’t help looking at him with varied expressions when it was revealed that the Night Riders were the ones sent after him, thanks to his ruthless reputation.
"What happened next?"

"We accepted the mission since we had already made plans to go after him long before the mission came. So all 69 of us prepared and embarked on this mission—a mission that would change everything we knew about the universe.

It took us ten years to track him down, and when we did, we attacked, and for thirty days, we fought. Within those thirty days, sixty-seven were injured to the point that raising their fingers was impossible.
The only ones that held on were the Veil Lady and me," Uncle Drew paused again and looked at Nara, giving her a smile.

"On the thirtieth day, she also fell, and on the thirty-first, I also reached my limit. It was the closest we came to death. However, instead of killing us, the Ruthless Bandit tattooed something on our bodies and left us.
Three days after he left, the Celestial Council sent another team to come and wipe us out. That team was later found out to be from the Soul Temple."
"What?" Kent was taken aback, his mind spinning as he tried to come to an understanding of what Uncle Drew was saying.
"Are you trying to say the Righteous Faction and the Soul Temple are in bed together?"

"No. But the Righteous Faction uses them occasionally to take care of all who aren’t walking in the line they had drawn. They just had to leak their location, and the Soul Temple would handle the rest.
Again, we survived because the Ruthless Bandit saw the betrayal coming and used us as bait to get his hands on the Soul Temple.
However, by saving us, both the Righteous Faction and the Soul Temple became his enemies. Years later, he became our leader because, just like him, they were after us too.
It took some time to adjust to his way of life.

As you all know and might have heard, the Ruthless Bandit was indeed a ruthless being. He doesn’t care how many he had to kill to get what he wanted... even if it meant killing the only daughter of the Supreme Celestial."
Yet again, the ladies turned and looked at Kent, causing him to blush... "I have no idea or memory that I did something like that. But even if I did, I am sure there is a reason for it... right?"
Uncle Drew smiled. "No, young master, you just felt like killing her to anger her father, and so you did."
"I guess I was a scum,"
"The biggest scum," Lene said with a giggle.

She used to fear the Ruthless Bandit, especially after she found out their battle with him was fought with half his strength. So now that Kent is all calm and innocent, she wouldn’t waste the chance to enjoy him while she still could.
"So by killing Lady Celestial, the Righteous Faction came after you and, in extension, us. For three hundred thousand years plus, we never had a moment of peace.
However, when the Dark Creatures came, and the universe was in danger, we stopped running and decided to fight. The Righteous Faction was occupied, so they stopped chasing us.
However, the Soul Temple didn’t stop. So at the climax of the battle, when you were locked in with the last Dark General, they struck.

You were so close to winning, but because of them, you lost the one advantage you had. With that advantage gone, it was either you die, and the universe perish, or you do the unthinkable and save the universe."
"What did I do?"
"Well, you did the unthinkable like always... Your death saved the universe, but it came at the expense of ours.
To kill the Dark General, you ignited your soul, and the blast killed both enemies and allies alike, which included the sixty-nine Night Riders."
"So I killed my own team," Kent said, his expression turning dull. Hearing he was the cause of the Night Riders’ deaths soured his mood.
"It is not that simple, young master. You were the only one who stood against seven Dark Generals. You killed six and were close to killing the seventh.
That time, the Righteous Faction had every chance to come to your aid. But because of their overinflated ego, they chose not to. In the end, it was either you die and let the universe fall into ruin.

Believe me, judging by how the universe had treated you, abandoning it was the most logical decision you could have made. But deep within you, that sense of justice still remained, so you made a decision, and it saved us all.
The universe stood, and we still lived, so there is no reason to blame you.
If it hadn’t been because of you, all sixty-nine of us would be dead or worse, imprisoned somewhere, undergoing torture over and over again.
So you saved the universe, and in return, saved us, too.
I am sure when you recall all your memories, everything will make sense."

"Uncle Drew is right."Lene stepped in, "You were many bad things, but there seems to be a reason for everything you did. Even killing Lady Celestial had proven how demented and rotten the Supreme Celestial was when he stood on the side and watched you endure all the load of the Dark Era.
He could have helped you carry some of the load. But he just stood on the side and watched everything come crashing down."
Kent nodded, then he vanished, appearing in the Sword Tower. None of his wives followed him because they knew he needed a moment to process what he had just learned.
He expected to hear the Soul Temple killed the Night Riders, as they claimed, but it seems he was the one who did the killing.
"AAAAAARRRGGHH"
His scream filled the Sword Tower...

chapters.title: Chapter 1394: Self-Hate
paragraphs: There is nothing any of his wives or legion is going to say that will stop Kent from blaming himself. He had killed the Night Riders, and while there may be a reason for all this, the fact that they died because of him made him feel terrible.
They are dead because of him. Even if he did it for a good reason, the point here is that they died, and he was the cause.
There is no denying that, and now that he knows, there is just nothing anyone can say that will change his mind.
The self-hate will grow in him for a while. But he will endure because while they died, they are now here, with him. That is something to be happy about.
Although he learned that he was at one point the leader of the Night Riders, he again didn’t expect them to meet on those terms.
They came to kill him, but from the way Uncle Drew spoke, it seemed he expected that outcome and was even ready for the betrayal that followed.
This indicated that he was intelligent. He devised a perfect plan that drew the Soul Temple into his scheme while leaving a good impression on the night riders.
The second was how powerful he truly was, to use just half his strength against the Night Riders.
Uncle Drew didn’t say how strong they were before facing him, but he knew from Vexthra that those who played the biggest role in the Dark War were the Night Riders.
So one can only imagine just how terrifying the Ruthless Bandit was to face such a team with only half his strength.

Kent had already met Chaos and saw how monstrous he was. He had already met Faceless, and while he was merely a demigod, he saw him assassinate gods, and perhaps he would be meeting many terrifying beings as he explored the Shadow Realm.
There is still more to learn about him.

But they aren’t the only ones whom he can say are dangerous. He had already seen what Jest could do with the sword, and so learning that the Ruthless Bandit was monstrous made him understand he was no simple person in all the lives he had lived.
But that’s nothing to be proud of now that he’s learned he was the cause of his own team’s death.
The memories he had recovered so far of the Ruthless Bandit point to a life of evil. He knew he would be extremely evil in that life, but how much evil would that be?
He just learned he killed an innocent lady simply because she was dear to someone he hated. To make that person bleed, he killed his innocent daughter.

That was just him being the scum of society, and he knew that. But even if he did it for a reason, like Lene said, the fact that he was able to cross that line was all he needed to know that he was a scum.
"I hope this all points to a bigger picture," he muttered, his head bowed as he sat beside the Sword of Enlightenment.
This won’t break him, but it will shape him in ways he would never see coming.
Meanwhile, back inside the legion tower, Vexthra and her sisters started thinking of what to do...
Kent’s mental health is their priority right now, so making sure he is happy is the only thing they can do.
"I still can’t believe the Righteous Faction tried to kill you guys," Velyra said, her expression filled with hatred toward the Righteous Faction.
"There are good people within their ranks. But at the end of the day, their leadership is rotten, and that can be said when they had every chance to aid the Ruthless Bandit but chose not to."

"That is indeed true. I was invited many times to join them, but refused not because I hated them, but because I hate the idea of someone dictating what I do with my life," Vexthra smirked. "Many gods had already joined them and are enjoying the benefits that come with it."
"That is true. I was also invited, but chose not to join them, not because I hate them, but because I already have a team.

They have some cool policies that you would love, but learning they stood on the side while the universe burned to the ground made me remember those thirteen scums who called themselves the universe guardians but ran when shit hit the fan during the Primordial Era."
Miryssa chuckled, feeling some form of disgust toward the Righteous Faction.

"The Ruthless Bandit was many evil things, but he was no hypocrite. He always has a reason for doing things if you examine his actions critically. However, it seems the young master would have to handle this on his own.
He didn’t know what truly happened, and to be frank, I don’t either. Back then, he had all the time in the world to send us away, but he didn’t.
His last words were, ’It had been a good run, guys, but now we must all die.’ The look on his face back then wasn’t that of someone who chose to kill us for fun.
So for now, I or any of you can’t help him. But we can hope that when he recovers his memories, he will find the reason why he did what he did.

As for the Righteous Faction, they should pray that the young master has more pressing things to handle. Trust me, when I recover my team, they will become our main target. They would pay for their transgressions. I am sure the Ruthless Bandit will come for them, too."
"What about the Soul Temple?" Neomi asked.
"From the records I found in the 14th level of Hell, the Soul Temple had lived since the Primordial Era. Some even say they were there during the Era of the Six True Primordials, so they run deep.
However, in the records, I learned that they faced their biggest adversary during the Divine Era."

Vexthra furrowed her brow. "Wasn’t that the era when the legendary Alchemist ruled the universe using wisdom and knowledge? I mean, he wasn’t a warrior or anything, so how can he bring such a formidable force to their knees?"
Uncle Drew smiled. "That was what the Righteous Faction wanted you to believe. In fact, while the universe saw the Ruthless Bandit as the most evil, that was because he showed his face as evil.
From the Hell records that I have reviewed, the legendary Pill Celestial Kevin Sage was someone the universe actually feared, not because he was evil. They feared him because he was too brilliant.
From the Hell records, there is an account of how he brought the Soul Temple to its knees. Nobody knew how, but he came close to wiping them out.
So the Ruthless Bandit will handle the Righteous Faction, and the legendary Divine Alchemist will take care of the Soul Temple."
Dia narrowed her eyes and then asked, "So in this scenario, does it mean Kent is or was the legendary Kevin Sage?"
Unity turned to her sister and replied, "If it isn’t him, then who else?"
"Unbelievable."

The ladies brainstormed everything they could, but in the end, they heeded Zaila’s advice and let Kent handle his own demons. He will be fine, but it would take time, so they chose not to disturb him.
Thankfully, after three days of back and forth, he calmed down and decided to apologize to the Night Riders.
They stopped him from doing that, but in the end, he did, and then he entered the Alchemy Tower to practice alchemy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1395: Pill Emperor
paragraphs: In the end, one can only put aside their grievances and work toward never making the same mistake ever again.

Kent put aside his pain, sorrow, and self-hate and chose to embrace the life ahead of him. He can only keep on moving forward and hope that one day, he will reach the point where he won’t have to worry about anything.
That one day, he would find out the truth.
Maybe then and only then can he stop hating himself.
Upon reaching the Alchemy tower, Kent headed straight to the Pill room, where his cauldron is always ready for him to make pills.
He had already reached the bottleneck to becoming a pill emperor. The only thing left for him to take the next step is to concoct a Tier 10 pill with a grey pill ring.

He had already concocted a Tier 9 pill with a grey pill ring. However, he must take it a step further now, and that is just not something he plans on failing at, not when he planned on becoming a Pill Monarch.
And if the requirements aren’t too much, he plans to become a Pill Sovereign and even a Pill Legend before the three years for him to head to Elina’s galaxy are up.𝕗𝗿𝕖𝐞𝐰𝗲𝕓𝐧𝕠𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝐨𝚖
This means he would be staying in the Pill tower for a while. His wives would have to head to the 9th floor and the subsequent ones without him.
He needs the time to take his mind off things, too.
So the moment he sat down, he retrieved the ingredients for the Mind Cleansing Pill. It is a pill said to give one clarity and calm their mind.
Naturally, he planned on doing drugs, so like the chemist he is, he would be cooking his own drug. Ain’t no better way to do drugs than if you are the chemist.
"Tower, how far is Nana coming with her seclusion?"

[Lady Nana had merged with 6 parts of her body. She has 4 more to go. At this rate, I track that she would be in seclusion for another decade or even more if she wants to return to her true form when everything is done.]
"Okay. Just keep a close eye on her and tell me if something changes."
[Okay, master.]
After retrieving all ten parts of her body that she had scattered across the 10-pill worlds, Nana entered seclusion to merge back with them and finally became the Apotheosis Cauldron, her true form.
Kent is more than happy to see what becomes of her once she is done.
Kent nodded and began heating the cauldron. Since he is inside the tower, he unleashed his Tier 16 soul flame and started heating the cauldron.
His soul flame is powerful enough to take him all the way to the rank of a Pill Legend, where he can make Tier 16 or even Tier 17 pills without much struggle.
So making a Tier 10 pill with a Tier 16 flame is overkill, and he knows that. However, that also didn’t mean he would have it easy. Tier 10 pills aren’t something an ordinary pill king can make.
In the vast universe, they are considered the start of pill making. Of course, in a High world, Tier 10 pills are highly sought after. However, immortals see it as a waste.

Even so, a Tier 10 pill with even a grey pill ring will catch the attention of even an Immortal. So Kent chose to go all out and make sure that when he is done with this seclusion, he will become a different kind of alchemist.
After heating the cauldron, he began the extraction process.
Extracting medicinal essence from a Tier 10 ingredient isn’t the same as extracting from a Tier 9, so he was being careful.
After an hour, he extracted the essence from all 14 ingredients. He then began burning impurities while condensing.

It took him another hour, a clear sign that the Tier 10 pill is vastly different from a Tier 9 pill. While he was able to do all this within an hour with the Tier 9 pill, it took him two good hours now.
Of course, he would learn to reduce that time to a more suitable one once he masters Tier 10 pill-making. But until then, he went ahead to condense and purify the pill.
However, while he expected a pure pill, he received a 90% pure one instead. This soured his mood, but he merely tossed it away and started a new batch of pill making.
That too came out 95% pure.
He didn’t frown this time, but he tossed it away and tried a third time. This time, he managed to get a pure pill within 3 hours, but had no more essence to attempt a pill ring refinement.
He didn’t toss this one away, but he didn’t consume it either.
Instead, he went in for a 4th trial, and for three hours, he worked on refining another pure pill. This time around, he managed to concoct a pure pill with a partial grey pill ring.
That was a great achievement.
"I suppose I took a huge leap, and it is plain now that I hold this pill in my hand. However, I also can’t help but wonder why things only seem to get more difficult as my understanding expands."
Kent looked at the pill in his hand for a few minutes before tossing it into his mouth. At once, his mind started to expand, or at least that was how it felt.
In actuality, his mind was rather clearing out space. It was making sure all unnecessary stuff was cleared for a much clearer thought to settle in.
So while his mind wasn’t expanding, he felt the space opening up like it was an expansion. This process took a couple of minutes, but when the pill had done its job, Kent felt refreshed.
He quickly started a new batch of pill making, making sure he took advantage of the clarity he had gained to think deeply into his understanding of alchemy.
Three hours later, he had achieved his goal.
⟦You have concocted a Tier 10 Mind Cleansing Pill. Purity: 100%, Pill Ring: Grey⟧
⟦You have fulfilled all the requirements to become a Pill Emperor⟧
⟦Congratulations, you are now a Pill Emperor⟧
The messages appeared, and a smile followed. However, he didn’t stop to see where he had to go next. Becoming a Pill Emperor is just the start.

He wants to be able to concoct a Tier 10 pill within an hour, so locking in for three days, he started making one pill after another, making sure every batch of pill making reduced the time taken to make the previous one.
It wasn’t easy, but after three days and a dozen times making the same pill, he had achieved an hour spent making a Tier 10 pill.
He spent another five days and a few hundred thousand tower points on pill ingredients to try his hand at other pills.
After making seven different pills in under an hour each, he finally decided to rest and see where he goes next.
He had just received knowledge of a Pill Emperor and the requirement to become a Pill Monarch, so he settled down under a tree to review those messages.

chapters.title: Chapter 1396: Next Requirements
paragraphs: At the Pill Emperor stage, Kent would have to master making Tier 11 and 12 pills before he could ascend to the rank of a Pill Monarch.
Unlike the Pill King stage, where he only concocted Tier 10 pills, the Pill Emperor stage is a bit different.
But he had received the knowledge of a Pill Emperor. He had received pill formulas and a whole lot that he could make good use of to master Tier 11 and 12 pill making.

Just like how he received the Pill King knowledge that aided him in making a Tier 10 pill to the point he even managed to refine a pill ring, he had yet again received such priceless knowledge, and that is just wonderful.
However, despite receiving this knowledge, there is an issue with the things contained in this piece of pill knowledge.
These changes made him understand that he may have previously underestimated what goes into pill-making.
To him, the mere fact that he was able to concoct a Tier 10 Mind Cleansing Pill means he can forever make more if he has the ingredients.
He believed he required only one recipe to make any rank of pill. Of course, in most cases, one requires only a single recipe for any rank of pill. But that isn’t always the case.
First, he discovered that, aside from merely having the recipe and ingredients, as a pill’s rank increases, the recipe can change too.
This means a recipe for Innate Talent awakening can change as the rank of the pill increases. The recipe for a Tier 5 pill is not the same as the recipe for a Tier 12 pill.
So the first thing he did was examine all the new recipes he had received and match them against what he already knew. The result was rather shocking.
Most of the recipes he knew had undergone changes that required more time to update, or else risk wasting ingredients and, to some extent, even his life.
Concocting the wrong pill can be dangerous most of the time. So he worked on updating his knowledge.
Once that was handled, he proceeded to his refinement techniques. He had received quite a few techniques and updates to the ones he already had.
Even the pill ring refinement art had undergone some qualitative upgrade.
After he handled that, he dove into the healing aspect of an Alchemist and updated his knowledge there, too.
It is not always about knowing the right pill; knowing which pill to use to cure a disease is also important.
In the end, he made sure his understanding of alchemy as a Pill Emperor was on point.
It was only then that he turned to the requirements to become a Pill Monarch.
⟦Requirement to become a Pill Monarch⟧
↠ Concoct a Tier 11 pill with a grey pill ring
↠ Concoct a Tier 12 pill with a grey pill ring
↠ Concoct any pill between the ranks of Tier 10 to 12 with an Azure Pill Ring
A pale smile appeared on Kent’s face. "I knew things wouldn’t be rainbows and sunshine, but who would have expected a Pill Emperor to attempt refining the Azure Pill Ring?"

Kent laughed, reading through the knowledge he had received from the Pill Celestial Kevin Sage. From what he could siphon from the knowledge, it was impossible to refine an azure pill ring for any pill below Tier 13.
That is just not possible.

To be able to attempt that, he needs more essence-rich ingredients, which can only be found from Tier 13 and upward. Tier 12 and below don’t have enough vitality to have the necessary essence to even attempt such a thing.

So, asking him to attempt such a thing and even have the audacity to recommend as low as a Tier 10 pill is just telling him to stop dreaming, that he would never become a Pill Monarch in this life or the next.
"If Pill Celestial Kevin Sage said it is impossible, who am I to argue?" Kent grinned and started reading through the techniques he had received again.
He paid more attention to those that can aid him in extracting the medicinal essence from the ingredients and those used for burning impurities.
Before he even starts to think about refining an Azure pill ring, he must master extracting pill essence to the most perfect state.
He must master extracting medicinal essence from any ingredient to the point that not even an atom of impurity will be in it.
And well, while that is also impossible to some degree, many legendary alchemists have achieved it before, so he can try to do so as well.
If he manages to extract all essence from ingredients, technically, he can attempt refining an azure pill ring.
But even if he can’t do that, he can attempt the next best option, which is making sure he can burn impurities without burning even a single drop of essence.
That too is impossible, but doable to some extent.
If he wants to even have an inkling chance of refining an Azure pill ring, then he must master one of these two, or both if possible.
But before that, there is a lot he must learn.
"I need to go back and start the process from a Tier 1 pill. If I want to perform a 100% extraction, I need to start from the basics and work my way up.
Once that is achieved at the Tier 10 stage, I will move to Tier 11 and then Tier 12. When all that is done, I will move to impurity burning, which I will follow with the same process.
I have all the time and resources, so there is no need to be stingy about this. I need to become someone whose knowledge of alchemy is not limited to what I inherited from my past life.
If Pill Celestial Kevin Sage said it is impossible, I will make it happen. Who knows, I might just become a legend in pill making, even surpassing my past self."

Kent laughed, then he started arranging the kinds of pills he would be working with. He must make sure he achieves what he was after with more than one pill. Only then would he be happy if he succeeded.
Two hours later, thousands of pill ingredients filled the pill room. He spent 20 million tower points purchasing all kinds of pill ingredients for ten different pills.
Since he is now swimming in tower points, he cut no corners, making sure he went all in and hoped he achieved what he was after in the end.
If he wants to become a Pill Monarch, he must do the impossible.
After he rested for three days, he started from Tier 1 again, this time putting all his thoughts into pill making.

It will take him a couple of trials to achieve what he is after, but at least that will make him happy in the end. He is obsessed with the sword simply because, a long time ago, he was all about becoming a swordsman.
He had already seen how much he put into mastering his swordsmanship, so he understood his obsession.
Now, he had to become obsessed with alchemy simply because he was once obsessed with it. He may not have the memories of that life, but he has the knowledge he has built over the years.
If he can put the same obsession into pill-making as he did with swordsmanship, then who knows what he would achieve with alchemy?
He already has the knowledge; the only thing left is to make sure he masters those methods and develops his own way of using them to accomplish his goal.
It wouldn’t be too late to consider creating his own refining techniques based on the knowledge he has so far.
